nodes.name: Quest
nodes.def: Protagonist searches for a specific person, place, or thing she believes will change her life; the object matters, unlike a mere plot device.
nodes.seat_why: 'Quest' — a searched-for object driving the whole external plot, not a two-person argument; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Adventure
nodes.def: Hero undertakes a journey for its own sake; the physical journey itself is the focus, not who the hero becomes along the way.
nodes.seat_why: 'Adventure' — the physical journey itself is the story's engine, explicitly not who the hero becomes; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Pursuit
nodes.def: One character chases another; suspense comes from proximity, cleverness, and near-misses between hunter and hunted.
nodes.seat_why: 'Pursuit' — a hunter/hunted dynamic between two parties is the whole pattern; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Rescue
nodes.def: Hero chases an antagonist to save a victim, a three-cornered plot built on protagonist, victim, and antagonist.
nodes.seat_why: 'Rescue' — a three-cornered rescue is defined by the protagonist's relationship to the one saved; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Escape
nodes.def: Protagonist is physically confined against her will and must break free; literal captivity, not a psychological trap.
nodes.seat_why: 'Escape' — confinement by an external system/captor, not an interpersonal argument; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Revenge
nodes.def: Protagonist retaliates against an antagonist for a real or imagined injury, retaliation usually falling outside the law.
nodes.seat_why: 'Revenge' — retaliation is a standing dyad between protagonist and the one who wronged her; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: The Riddle
nodes.def: A mystery built on a deliberately ambiguous question whose hidden meaning the protagonist must decode.
nodes.seat_why: 'The Riddle' — a mystery to decode is an external-plot engine; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Rivalry
nodes.def: Two evenly matched characters compete for the same goal or object, each with her own strong motivation.
nodes.seat_why: 'Rivalry' — two evenly matched rivals competing for one goal is the textbook RS pattern; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Underdog
nodes.def: A rivalry plot where the protagonist is badly outmatched and must overcome overwhelming odds against a superior antagonist.
nodes.seat_why: 'Underdog' — an underdog rivalry is the Rivalry pattern with the odds skewed; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Temptation
nodes.def: Protagonist is induced or persuaded toward something unwise, wrong, or immoral, and must choose whether to yield.
nodes.seat_why: 'Temptation' — being induced or persuaded toward something unwise is textbook pressure-from-another; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Metamorphosis
nodes.def: A character literally changes physical shape, the transformation reflecting the inner psychological identity of the metamorph.
nodes.seat_why: 'Metamorphosis' — a literal shape-change reflecting inner identity is an MC-pattern by the pattern's own def; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Transformation
nodes.def: Closely related to metamorphosis, but the character's change is psychological rather than a literal change of shape.
nodes.seat_why: 'Transformation' — psychological change in the protagonist, no relationship or faction implicated; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Maturation
nodes.def: Protagonist passes from childhood innocence toward adult understanding, gaining hard-won, often disillusioning knowledge of the world.
nodes.seat_why: 'Maturation' — the protagonist's own passage from innocence to understanding; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Love
nodes.def: Two people fall in love but face an obstacle ('Boy meets girl, but...') that must be overcome before union.
nodes.seat_why: 'Love' — two people falling in love against an obstacle is the RS pattern by definition; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Forbidden Love
nodes.def: A love affair violates a social taboo such as race, rank, incest, or adultery, and must survive society's judgment.
nodes.seat_why: 'Forbidden Love' — a love affair is still the RS argument, now also indicted by the OS/society's taboo; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Sacrifice
nodes.def: Protagonist gives up someone or something valued, the concept rooted in offering something to a god to secure a bond.
nodes.seat_why: 'Sacrifice' — the protagonist's own capacity to give something up, an inner value choice; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Discovery
nodes.def: Protagonist searches for self-knowledge, pursuing some version of 'who am I, why am I here.'
nodes.seat_why: 'Discovery' — self-knowledge, 'who am I,' is the MC's inner question by definition; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Wretched Excess
nodes.def: Protagonist pushes past the limits of acceptable behavior into extremity, by choice or by accident, fascinating for living at the margins.
nodes.seat_why: 'Wretched Excess' — the protagonist's own drift past behavioral limits, an inner-arc pattern; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Ascension
nodes.def: Protagonist's spiritual rise from a lower to a higher state, sinner to saint, a parable rather than a cautionary tale.
nodes.seat_why: 'Ascension' — spiritual rise from a lower to higher state is an inner-change pattern; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Descension
nodes.def: Protagonist's fall from a high place through a character flaw such as greed, pride, or lust; a cautionary tale.
nodes.seat_why: 'Descension' — a fall through the protagonist's own character flaw is an inner-change pattern; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Supplication
nodes.def: A Petitioner begs a Power in Authority for help against a Persecutor who blocks it; explores power, authority, and how need is met.
nodes.seat_why: 'Supplication' — a Petitioner appealing to a Power in Authority stages a power/authority (factional) problem; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Benefaction
nodes.def: The opposite of Supplication: a character confers aid, a charitable gift, or goodwill on another, unasked, showing power justly used.
nodes.seat_why: 'Benefaction' — the mirror of Supplication, same authority/power axis; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Deliverance
nodes.def: An unexpected protector (Rescuer) frees an Unfortunate from a Threatener's danger without having been asked for help first.
nodes.seat_why: 'Deliverance' — a rescuer-unfortunate dyad, the relationship that undoes the threat; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Sojourn
nodes.def: A stranger visits rather than rescues; his presence enriches or unsettles a family or community, without a life-or-death stake.
nodes.seat_why: 'Sojourn' — a stranger's mere presence pressuring/unsettling a family is classic influence-character pressure; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Vengeance for a Crime
nodes.def: An Avenger who feels sympathy or duty toward a Victim seeks to punish a Criminal, often taking justice outside the law.
nodes.seat_why: 'Vengeance for a Crime' — avenger and criminal form the whole pattern, a standing two-party grievance; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Rehabilitation
nodes.def: The Avenger becomes a Rehabilitator who tries to reform the Criminal rather than punish him, often at the Victim's own request.
nodes.seat_why: 'Rehabilitation' — the same avenger/criminal dyad, redirected toward reform; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Vengeance Taken for Kindred Upon Kindred
nodes.def: Like Vengeance for a Crime, but the Avenging Kinsman, Guilty Kinsman, and Victim are all related by blood or marriage.
nodes.seat_why: 'Vengeance Taken for Kindred Upon Kindred' — vengeance narrowed to kin, still a two-party (now blood-bound) dyad; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Appearance of a New Kinsman
nodes.def: A new relative appears and is welcomed into the clan, the Avenging Kinsman becoming a Protecting Kinsman instead.
nodes.seat_why: 'Appearance of a New Kinsman' — a new relative's welcome is a kinship-relationship pattern; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Flight
nodes.def: The main character runs, flees, or makes a hasty departure; focus stays on the one escaping, not the pursuer.
nodes.seat_why: 'Flight' — focus stays on the one escaping — her own state, not a chase relationship; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Pursuit
nodes.def: The Fugitive becomes the Pursuer, striving toward a goal — a person, activity, or self-improvement — against an obstacle.
nodes.seat_why: 'Pursuit' — striving toward a goal or self-improvement is the protagonist's own inner-directed arc; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Disaster
nodes.def: A catastrophe or grave misfortune strikes a Vanquished Power, playing on the basic human fear of the unknown.
nodes.seat_why: 'Disaster' — a catastrophe striking a Vanquished Power is external/societal, the fear of the unknown at scale; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Miracle
nodes.def: An unexplainable, spontaneous event reverses a Vanquished Power's fortune, the mirror of Disaster.
nodes.seat_why: 'Miracle' — the mirror of Disaster, same external/societal axis; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Falling Prey to Cruelty or Misfortune
nodes.def: An Unfortunate suffers repeated, unforeseen trouble at the hands of a Master or of circumstance, a pessimistic, melodramatic situation.
nodes.seat_why: 'Falling Prey to Cruelty or Misfortune' — trouble at the hands of a Master is pressure exerted by another onto the Unfortunate; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Becoming Fortunate
nodes.def: Unexpected good luck reverses a needy character's fate, the Unfortunate becoming Fortunate out of nowhere.
nodes.seat_why: 'Becoming Fortunate' — the same Master/Unfortunate axis, reversed to good luck; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Revolt
nodes.def: A Conspirator attempts to overthrow the authority of a Tyrant; unlike the previous pair, this concerns a group rather than one person.
nodes.seat_why: 'Revolt' — explicitly 'concerns a group rather than one person' — a factional/authority pattern; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Support
nodes.def: The Conspirator becomes a Supporter, backing the power he agrees with instead of revolting, implying a democratic option exists.
nodes.seat_why: 'Support' — the same group-vs-authority axis, redirected to backing the power; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Daring Enterprise
nodes.def: A Bold Leader undertakes a risky, complicated venture toward an Object against an Adversary; the personal type is 'similar to a Quest.'
nodes.seat_why: 'Daring Enterprise' — a Bold Leader's venture toward an Object against an Adversary is external-plot shaped, 'similar to a Quest'; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: The Healing Journey
nodes.def: The Bold Leader becomes a Healer whose inner journey is to heal herself or others, benefiting the community as she grows.
nodes.seat_why: 'The Healing Journey' — the Healer's is explicitly an inner journey to heal herself or others; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Abduction
nodes.def: A Guardian fails to prevent an Abductor from carrying off a Victim by force; a personal loss and failure of duty for the Guardian.
nodes.seat_why: 'Abduction' — Guardian and Victim form the standing dyad a failure of duty breaks; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Reunion
nodes.def: The Guardian becomes a Facilitator who helps the Victim reunite with someone dear, happily or with difficulty depending on mutual desire.
nodes.seat_why: 'Reunion' — the same Guardian/Victim dyad, now working toward reunion; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Enigma
nodes.def: An Interrogator and a Seeker confront a Problem that cannot be satisfactorily explained; the engine of mystery and riddle plots.
nodes.seat_why: 'Enigma' — explicitly 'the engine of mystery and riddle plots' — an external puzzle for the cast; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Invention
nodes.def: The Seeker becomes an Inventor, creating her own answer to an insurmountable problem no one else can solve for her.
nodes.seat_why: 'Invention' — the Seeker becoming her own Inventor is a self-directed, inner-resourced solution; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Obtaining
nodes.def: A Solicitor or Arbitrator works, through selling or negotiation, to acquire an object or objective as the result of planning.
nodes.seat_why: 'Obtaining' — acquiring an object through negotiation is an external, plan-driven goal; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Letting Go
nodes.def: The Solicitor becomes a Liberator, giving up what she has obtained to become freer, surrendering what ties her to unhappiness.
nodes.seat_why: 'Letting Go' — surrendering what was obtained to become freer is an inner-value reversal; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Enmity of Kinsman
nodes.def: A Malevolent Kinsman and a Hated Kinsman share deep, often mutual, hatred, reciprocal or one-sided.
nodes.seat_why: 'Enmity of Kinsman' — mutual hatred between kinsmen is a standing two-party dyad; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Hero to Kinsman
nodes.def: A younger kinsman admires and looks up to an older 'Heroic Idol,' who may mentor him or later be defended by him.
nodes.seat_why: 'Hero to Kinsman' — admiration/mentorship between kinsmen is the same dyad, warmer; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Competition
nodes.def: An Exceptional Person and an Adversary are equally, obsessively fixated on the same Object, more invested in the contest than the prize.
nodes.seat_why: 'Competition' — two people fixated on the same object/prize, obsessive rivalry; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Concession
nodes.def: The Exceptional Person becomes a Sacrificer who willingly lets the Adversary win the Object, secure enough not to need it.
nodes.seat_why: 'Concession' — the same rivalry dyad, resolved by willingly conceding; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Adultery
nodes.def: Two Adulterers betray a Betrayed Spouse in a voluntary relationship outside marriage; betrayal, not just infidelity, drives the conflict.
nodes.seat_why: 'Adultery' — two adulterers and a betrayed spouse — the argument is the relationship; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Fidelity
nodes.def: The Adulterer becomes a Faithful Spouse who refuses another lover after losing her spouse to death, prison, illness, or divorce.
nodes.seat_why: 'Fidelity' — the same triangle, resolved by fidelity instead; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Madness
nodes.def: A Madman menaces a Victim who may die early or struggle to survive; insanity read as a fearful mystery.
nodes.seat_why: 'Madness' — madness read as a menace is an inner-state pattern (paired with Genius); whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Genius
nodes.def: The Madman becomes a Genius, too smart and intense to fit the world, seeing and questioning what no one else does.
nodes.seat_why: 'Genius' — the same inner-state axis, reframed as genius; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Imprudence
nodes.def: An unwise, hasty act by the Imprudent character triggers a chain of escalating consequences for himself and others.
nodes.seat_why: 'Imprudence' — an unwise, hasty act is the protagonist's own trait driving consequences; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Caution
nodes.def: The Imprudent becomes the Cautious, taking time over decisions, secure enough to act, or not act, without pressure.
nodes.seat_why: 'Caution' — the same trait axis, reframed as caution; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Crimes of Love
nodes.def: A Lover commits a crime with a Beloved, voluntary or involuntary, a crime of the heart that society treats as taboo.
nodes.seat_why: 'Crimes of Love' — a lover and beloved's crime is a relationship pattern, judged by the outside world; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Sacrifice for Love
nodes.def: The Lover becomes a Sacrificer, giving up his own needs for the Beloved's well-being, at peace even at a distance.
nodes.seat_why: 'Sacrifice for Love' — the same lover/beloved dyad, resolved by sacrifice instead of crime; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Slaying of a Loved One
nodes.def: A Slayer must kill a Victim who turns out to be, or is already known to be, a relative, for a stated Reason.
nodes.seat_why: 'Slaying of a Loved One' — a slayer and a loved-one victim — the relationship is the whole horror of the pattern; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Conviction
nodes.def: The Slayer becomes a Challenger who questions the vows and orders that demand he slay another, refusing blind obedience.
nodes.seat_why: 'Conviction' — the same slayer axis, redirected into refusing the order; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Self-Sacrifice
nodes.def: A Hero gives up a Thing Sacrificed, out of passion, ideal, or duty to kindred, in a noble, unselfish act.
nodes.seat_why: 'Self-Sacrifice' — giving up a thing sacrificed out of passion or duty is an inner, self-directed act; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Self-Preservation
nodes.def: The Hero becomes a Preserver who protects herself from harm, valuing her own life and refusing to give it up without a fight.
nodes.seat_why: 'Self-Preservation' — the same inner axis, reframed as self-preservation; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Discovery of the Dishonor of a Loved One
nodes.def: A Discoverer uncovers the shame of a loved one, current or hidden from the past, testing his loyalty and compassion.
nodes.seat_why: 'Discovery of the Dishonor of a Loved One' — a Discoverer's loyalty to a loved one is tested by what's uncovered — the relationship is the stake; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Discovery of the Honor of a Loved One
nodes.def: The Discoverer learns a loved one he misjudged as shameful was in fact honorable, and must make amends for the misjudgment.
nodes.seat_why: 'Discovery of the Honor of a Loved One' — the same Discoverer/loved-one dyad, reversed to vindication; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Obstacles to Love
nodes.def: Two Lovers are kept apart, or nearly so, by an Obstacle, and attempt to surmount whatever is thrown in their path.
nodes.seat_why: 'Obstacles to Love' — two lovers kept apart by an obstacle is the textbook RS pattern; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Unconditional Love
nodes.def: A Lover is so overwhelmed by being loved absolutely and without condition that he may take years to accept the gift.
nodes.seat_why: 'Unconditional Love' — unconditional love between two people is the same axis, deepened; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Conflict With a God
nodes.def: A Mortal stands in disharmony with an Immortal, staging religious and spiritual questions through their conflict.
nodes.seat_why: 'Conflict With a God' — a mortal's disharmony with an immortal stages religious/spiritual questions at large, not one relationship; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Supernatural Occurrence
nodes.def: The Mortal becomes a Gifted One (Receiver or Witness) who touches powers outside the natural world.
nodes.seat_why: 'Supernatural Occurrence' — the same cosmic axis, reframed as a gifted touch of the supernatural; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Mistaken Judgment
nodes.def: A Mistaken One wrongly judges a Victim, out of jealousy, false suspicion, or an Instigator's manipulation.
nodes.seat_why: 'Mistaken Judgment' — a mistaken judgment is the judging character's own cognitive/inner failure; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Intuitive Judgment
nodes.def: The Mistaken One becomes the Intuitive One, who knows the truth without rational process, seeing past the obvious clues.
nodes.seat_why: 'Intuitive Judgment' — the same inner axis, reframed as intuitive judgment; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Remorse
nodes.def: A Culprit suffers suppressed guilt over a Victim or sin, needing people or events to force his eyes open.
nodes.seat_why: 'Remorse' — suppressed guilt is an inner emotional state needing to surface; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Empathy
nodes.def: The Culprit becomes an Empath who feels others' pain so deeply that she becomes incapable of committing harm.
nodes.seat_why: 'Empathy' — the same inner axis, reframed as empathy; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Loss of a Loved One
nodes.def: A Kinsman Spectator mourns a Kinsman Slain by an Executioner, the situation built entirely around grief.
nodes.seat_why: 'Loss of a Loved One' — a spectator mourning a slain kinsman is grief built entirely around the kinship relationship; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Rescue of a Loved One
nodes.def: The Kinsman Spectator becomes a Rescuing Kinsman, able to gather resources and act instead of standing by helpless.
nodes.seat_why: 'Rescue of a Loved One' — the same kinship dyad, redirected into active rescue; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Odd Couple
nodes.def: A Hero and a close Opposite Hero, utterly different, are forced together by an Event and must learn to work as one.
nodes.seat_why: 'Odd Couple' — a forced pairing of opposites who must learn to work as one is a two-person dynamic by definition; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Fish Out of Water
nodes.def: A misfit Hero cannot adjust to her environment or circumstances, whether from real displacement or simple self-doubt.
nodes.seat_why: 'Fish Out of Water' — a misfit's inability to adjust is her own inner/displacement state, not a two-person argument; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Blank Situation Template
nodes.def: Not a named dramatic situation but a blank worksheet the book offers so a writer can define her own 56th situation.
nodes.seat_why: 'Blank Situation Template' — explicitly a blank worksheet, not a named situation — no fit by design; whole-plot pattern, act 'any' (rides the walk's current signpost).

nodes.name: Absentation
nodes.def: A member of a family absents himself from home (work, war, trade, or death), removing a protective presence.
nodes.seat_why: 'Absentation' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 1 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Interdiction
nodes.def: An interdiction or warning is addressed to the hero, telling him what not to do.
nodes.seat_why: 'Interdiction' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 1 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Violation
nodes.def: The interdiction is violated, opening the way for the villain to act.
nodes.seat_why: 'Violation' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 1 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Reconnaissance
nodes.def: The villain attempts reconnaissance, trying to find the location of children or valuables, or seeking out his victim.
nodes.seat_why: 'Reconnaissance' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 1 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Delivery
nodes.def: The villain receives information about his victim, often because the victim unwittingly answers his questions.
nodes.seat_why: 'Delivery' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 1 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Trickery
nodes.def: The villain attempts to deceive his victim in order to take possession of the victim or his belongings.
nodes.seat_why: 'Trickery' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 1 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Complicity
nodes.def: The victim submits to deception and thereby unwittingly helps his enemy.
nodes.seat_why: 'Complicity' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 1 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Villainy
nodes.def: The villain causes harm or injury to a member of a family: abduction, theft, injury, or murder; a paired alternate form is simple lack.
nodes.seat_why: 'Villainy' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 1 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Mediation, the connective incident
nodes.def: Misfortune or lack is made known; the hero is approached with a request or command, and is allowed to go or is dispatched.
nodes.seat_why: 'Mediation, the connective incident' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 1 of Propp's own function order (same_as Campbell/Vogler Call to Adventure, Act1).

nodes.name: Beginning Counteraction
nodes.def: The seeker-hero agrees to, or decides upon, counteraction against the villain.
nodes.seat_why: 'Beginning Counteraction' — hero's own decision/reaction, not a whole-cast event; act 2 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Departure
nodes.def: The hero leaves home to begin the search or the journey proper.
nodes.seat_why: 'Departure' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 2 of Propp's own function order (same_as Campbell/Vogler Crossing the Threshold, Act2).

nodes.name: First Function of the Donor
nodes.def: The hero is tested, interrogated, or attacked, preparing the way for his receiving a magical agent or helper.
nodes.seat_why: 'First Function of the Donor' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 2 of Propp's own function order (same_as Campbell/Vogler donor stage, Act2).

nodes.name: The Hero's Reaction
nodes.def: The hero reacts to the actions of the future donor, passing or failing the test set for him.
nodes.seat_why: 'The Hero's Reaction' — hero's own decision/reaction, not a whole-cast event; act 2 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Provision of a Magical Agent
nodes.def: The hero acquires the use of a magical agent, received as a gift, made, purchased, or otherwise obtained.
nodes.seat_why: 'Provision of a Magical Agent' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 2 of Propp's own function order (same_as Campbell/Vogler donor stage, Act2).

nodes.name: Spatial Transference
nodes.def: The hero is transferred, delivered, or led to the whereabouts of the object of his search.
nodes.seat_why: 'Spatial Transference' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 2 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Struggle
nodes.def: The hero and the villain join in direct combat.
nodes.seat_why: 'Struggle' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 3 of Propp's own function order (same_as Vogler Ordeal, Act3).

nodes.name: Branding
nodes.def: The hero is branded or marked, on the body or given an object, that will later identify him.
nodes.seat_why: 'Branding' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 3 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Victory
nodes.def: The villain is defeated, in open combat or by cleverness, sometimes with the villain hiding and a substitute punished instead.
nodes.seat_why: 'Victory' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 3 of Propp's own function order (same_as Vogler Ordeal, Act3).

nodes.name: Liquidation
nodes.def: The initial misfortune or lack is liquidated: the sought-for object is seized, a spell broken, or a captive freed.
nodes.seat_why: 'Liquidation' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 3 of Propp's own function order (same_as Campbell Ultimate Boon / Vogler Reward, Act3).

nodes.name: Return
nodes.def: The hero returns home or continues onward, the beginning of the tale's second half.
nodes.seat_why: 'Return' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order (same_as Campbell Magic Flight / Vogler Road Back, Act4).

nodes.name: Pursuit, chase
nodes.def: The hero is pursued by the villain or another threatening pursuer.
nodes.seat_why: 'Pursuit, chase' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Rescue of the Hero from Pursuit
nodes.def: The hero is rescued from pursuit, escaping the chase by aid, disguise, or obstacle.
nodes.seat_why: 'Rescue of the Hero from Pursuit' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Unrecognized Arrival
nodes.def: The hero, unrecognized, arrives home or in another country.
nodes.seat_why: 'Unrecognized Arrival' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Unfounded Claims
nodes.def: A false hero presents unfounded claims to the reward or the object of the quest.
nodes.seat_why: 'Unfounded Claims' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Difficult Task
nodes.def: A difficult task is proposed to the hero, a further trial before recognition.
nodes.seat_why: 'Difficult Task' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Solution
nodes.def: The task is resolved by the hero.
nodes.seat_why: 'Solution' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Recognition
nodes.def: The hero is recognized, usually by a mark, brand, or token left earlier.
nodes.seat_why: 'Recognition' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Exposure
nodes.def: The false hero or villain is exposed.
nodes.seat_why: 'Exposure' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Transfiguration
nodes.def: The hero is given a new appearance, a magical change of visible form.
nodes.seat_why: 'Transfiguration' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Punishment
nodes.def: The villain is punished.
nodes.seat_why: 'Punishment' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Wedding
nodes.def: The hero is married and/or ascends the throne.
nodes.seat_why: 'Wedding' — a plot function that plays across hero, villain, and donor alike; act 4 of Propp's own function order.

nodes.name: Ordinary World
nodes.def: The hero's normal life and world are established before any call arrives, the baseline the coming adventure will disrupt.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'Ordinary World' — The hero's normal life and world are established before any call arrives; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 1, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: Call to Adventure
nodes.def: A problem, challenge, or opportunity confronts the hero, unbalancing the ordinary world and inviting her into the story.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'Call to Adventure' — A problem; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 1, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: Refusal of the Call
nodes.def: The hero hesitates or refuses out of fear, insecurity, or duty, voicing the risks the journey will demand.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'Refusal of the Call' — The hero hesitates or refuses out of fear; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 1, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: Meeting with the Mentor
nodes.def: The hero encounters a wise figure who trains, equips, or advises him before he commits to the threshold.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'Meeting with the Mentor' — The hero encounters a wise figure who trains; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 2, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: Crossing the First Threshold
nodes.def: The hero commits and leaves the ordinary world behind, entering the special world of the adventure proper.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'Crossing the First Threshold' — The hero commits and leaves the ordinary world behind; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 2, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: Tests, Allies, Enemies
nodes.def: The hero learns the rules of the special world through trials, and sorts out who can be trusted and who cannot.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'Tests, Allies, Enemies' — The hero learns the rules of the special world through trials; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 2, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: Approach to the Inmost Cave
nodes.def: The hero nears the most dangerous place in the special world, making final preparations for the central ordeal.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'Approach to the Inmost Cave' — The hero nears the most dangerous place in the special world; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 3, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: The Ordeal
nodes.def: The hero faces a life-or-death crisis, a symbolic death and rebirth that is the central crisis of the story.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'The Ordeal' — The hero faces a life-or-death crisis; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 3, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: Reward
nodes.def: Having survived the ordeal, the hero seizes the sword: takes possession of the goal or a hard-won gift.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'Reward' — Having survived the ordeal; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 3, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: The Road Back
nodes.def: The hero commits to finishing the adventure and returning to the ordinary world, often pursued by consequences of the ordeal.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'The Road Back' — The hero commits to finishing the adventure and returning to the ordinary world; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 4, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: The Resurrection
nodes.def: A second, harder death-and-rebirth test purifies the hero before he is allowed to fully return.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'The Resurrection' — A second; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 4, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: Return with the Elixir
nodes.def: The hero comes home transformed, bringing something of value back to share with the ordinary world.
nodes.seat_why: Hero-journey stage 'Return with the Elixir' — The hero comes home transformed; MC by default (own inner journey); quartered 3-per-act, act 4, cross-checked against Campbell/Propp same_as anchors.

nodes.name: Call to Adventure
nodes.def: A herald or chance event signals that destiny has summoned the hero, the familiar life horizon about to be outgrown.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'Call to Adventure' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 1 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: Refusal of the Call

nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'Refusal of the Call' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 1 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: Supernatural Aid
nodes.def: A protective figure, often an old man or woman, appears to give the hero amulets or counsel for the trials ahead.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'Supernatural Aid' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 2 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: The Crossing of the First Threshold
nodes.def: The hero passes the guardian at the edge of the known world into the zone of the unknown.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'The Crossing of the First Threshold' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 2 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: The Belly of the Whale
nodes.def: The hero is swallowed into the unknown, a symbolic death and passage into a sphere of rebirth.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'The Belly of the Whale' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 3 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: The Road of Trials

nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'The Road of Trials' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 3 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: The Meeting with the Goddess
nodes.def: The hero experiences a mystical marriage with the queen goddess of the world, the ultimate adventure of the heart.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'The Meeting with the Goddess' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 3 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: Woman as the Temptress
nodes.def: The hero meets temptation that can turn him from his path, abundance recast as a trap for the flesh or spirit.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'Woman as the Temptress' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 3 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: Atonement with the Father
nodes.def: The hero confronts and reconciles with the ultimate power that has held dominion over his life, often a father figure.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'Atonement with the Father' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 3 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: Apotheosis
nodes.def: The hero rests in a godlike state of understanding and peace, a pause of divine knowledge before the final labor.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'Apotheosis' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 3 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: The Ultimate Boon
nodes.def: The hero achieves the goal of the quest, the life-transmuting trophy sought since the call to adventure.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'The Ultimate Boon' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 3 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: Refusal of the Return
nodes.def: Having found bliss in the other world, the hero may refuse to return to ordinary life.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'Refusal of the Return' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 4 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: The Magic Flight
nodes.def: If the boon was seized against opposition, the hero must flee in a hair-breadth escape, aided or pursued magically.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'The Magic Flight' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 4 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: Rescue from Without
nodes.def: The hero must sometimes be brought back from the adventure by helpers reaching in from the ordinary world.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'Rescue from Without' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 4 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: The Crossing of the Return Threshold
nodes.def: The hero must retain the wisdom of the deep and reconcile it with the world of common day.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'The Crossing of the Return Threshold' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 4 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

nodes.name: Master of the Two Worlds
nodes.def: The hero gains the freedom to pass back and forth between the worlds of spirit and of everyday life.
nodes.seat_why: Monomyth stage 'Master of the Two Worlds' — MC by default (hero's own journey); act 4 of Campbell's own Departure/Threshold/Initiation/Return arc, held to the same boundary as its Vogler/Propp same_as equivalents.

tropes.name: A Deadly Affair
tropes.def: An extramarital affair that leads to murder.

tropes.name: A Fool and His New Money Are Soon Parted
tropes.def: A character becomes rich, but then ends up losing their wealth.

tropes.name: A Friend in Need
tropes.def: A character proves their loyalty and friendship by helping their friend when it would be easier not to and other people would not blame them for not doing so.

tropes.name: A Hero Is Born
tropes.def: The story begins with the hero's birth or infancy.

tropes.name: A Match Made in Stockholm
tropes.def: The pair meet when one kidnaps the other.

tropes.name: A Minor Kidroduction
tropes.def: A work begins with a brief scene of the protagonist as a child.

tropes.name: A Real Man Is a Killer
tropes.def: A man discovers that he must kill something in order to prove his worth.

tropes.name: A Simple Plan
tropes.def: The characters come up with an easy straightforward plan, only for it to fall apart.

tropes.name: Abortion Fallout Drama
tropes.def: Plotline focusing on how getting an abortion affects the character and her relationships.

tropes.name: Abuse Mistake
tropes.def: Something innocent is mistaken for abuse or vice-versa.

tropes.name: Accidental Athlete
tropes.def: Someone discovers their athletic ability while doing something else.

tropes.name: Accidental Hero
tropes.def: A person performs a heroic action by complete accident.

tropes.name: Accidental Marriage
tropes.def: Someone gets married accidentally.

tropes.name: Achilles in His Tent
tropes.def: A powerful team member quits, but returns to save the day just as the team needs their specific talents.

tropes.name: Time out just before the big battle
tropes.def: The Heroes gather around a campfire and prepare for the battle, tell stories, confess their feelings, etc. It reminds them of what's at stake, and serves as a breather after all the action of the Road of Trials.

tropes.name: Actually a Doombot
tropes.def: The villain the hero was fighting turns out to be a robot double or clone of the real villain.

tropes.name: Adventure Rebuff
tropes.def: One character tries to keep another character out of trouble by forbidding them to go on missions with him, which never works.

tropes.name: Adventures in the Bible
tropes.def: Time travel to events from religion or mythology.

tropes.name: After-Adventure Restoration
tropes.def: A person is restored, as much as possible, to how they were before they went on an adventure.

tropes.name: Against the Grain
tropes.def: A character doesn't fulfil their expected role.

tropes.name: Alien Among Us
tropes.def: An alien living with a bunch of humans and trying to keep their alienness secret.

tropes.name: Alien Invasion
tropes.def: Aliens plan to invade a planet.

tropes.name: All for Nothing
tropes.def: A story's buildup gets its payoff. A later event renders it meaningless.

tropes.name: All Is Well That Ends Well
tropes.def: A character goes through a lot of hardship and strife, but once they get their happy ending they appear completely unaffected by this.

tropes.name: All That Glitters
tropes.def: Expected treasure turns out to be worthless.

tropes.name: All Up to You
tropes.def: An Unlikely Hero is the only one who can solve the problem.

tropes.name: All Your Base Are Belong to Us
tropes.def: The villains take over the hero's lair.

tropes.name: Allegory Adventure
tropes.def: A creative work in which the characters, plot, or both parallel those in another creative work.

tropes.name: Amateur Film-Making Plot
tropes.def: Characters try to create a low budget film.

tropes.name: America Saves the Day
tropes.def: A world-wide problem is solved by the United States.

tropes.name: Amnesia Danger
tropes.def: A character would be able to deal with this easily if they had their memories. Unfortunately, they don't.

tropes.name: An Offer You Can't Refuse
tropes.def: An offer where the choices are, "Accept or die"

tropes.name: And Now You Must Marry Me
tropes.def: The villain tries to force a protagonist to marry them.

tropes.name: And the Adventure Continues
tropes.def: The story ends with the heroes preparing for another adventure.

tropes.name: Anguished Declaration of Love
tropes.def: ...with great angst.

tropes.name: Animal Testing
tropes.def: The controversial act of testing medicine on animals.

tropes.name: Antagonist in Mourning
tropes.def: The villain feels sorry for the hero's death.

tropes.name: Anti-School Uniforms Plot
tropes.def: A group of students protest a newly installed rule requiring school uniforms.

tropes.name: Apocalypse Wow
tropes.def: The apocalypse is absolutely nightmarish, but man if it isn't cool!

tropes.name: Apophenia Plot
tropes.def: A character misinteprets a series of events and thinks they see a conspiracy where none exists.

tropes.name: Appease the Volcano God
tropes.def: A group try to throw a character into a volcano to appease the volcano god.

tropes.name: Ascend to a Higher Plane of Existence
Asinine Alternate Activity
tropes.def: A character isn't allowed to do something they want, with a boring alternative offered instead.

tropes.name: Assimilation Plot
tropes.def: A villain attempts to eliminate all differences between people.

tropes.name: Attack of the Town Festival
tropes.def: A town holding a festival is under attack.

tropes.name: Awesome Achievement, Petty Purpose
tropes.def: Someone's motivation for building a great invention or achieving a difficult goal turns out to be pretty petty.

tropes.name: Awesome Moment of Crowning
tropes.def: Story ends with character being crowned ruler of the land they just saved.

tropes.name: Awkward First Sleepover
tropes.def: A socially awkward child, teen or adult attends their first sleepover.

tropes.name: Axes at School
tropes.def: Someone brings a weapon to class.

tropes.name: Babies Ever After
tropes.def: The story ends with the heroes having children.

tropes.name: Back for the Finale
tropes.def: A character who hasn't been seen in a while returns at the end of the series.

tropes.name: Back to School
tropes.def: An adult character returns to school.

tropes.name: Bad Samaritan
tropes.def: Someone takes in the hero and seems (at first) to be helping, but they have ulterior motives.

tropes.name: Bad Santa
tropes.def: Santa Claus has either gone bad or has a villainous impostor or rival.

tropes.name: Badass in Distress
tropes.def: An Action Hero finds themself in the role of a Damsel in Distress / Distressed Dude .

tropes.name: Bait Audience Surrogate
tropes.def: The relatable blank-slate main character isn't as relatable as we thought.

tropes.name: Band Episode
tropes.def: The characters form a band or a musical group.

tropes.name: Bathe Her and Bring Her to Me
tropes.def: The villain has the damsel cleaned up before... well, you know.

tropes.name: Batman in My Basement
tropes.def: A character hides out in someone's home. One resident has to keep the others from finding out.

tropes.name: Be Careful What You Wish For
tropes.def: Someone makes a wish and finds out the hard way that their desire has its downsides.

tropes.name: Be Yourself
tropes.def: Someone tries to change who they are to accomplish their goal or so that people will like them better. They learn in the end that they're fine just the way they are.

tropes.name: Becoming the Costume
tropes.def: People are turned into whatever they're dressed to be.

tropes.name: Becoming the Genie
tropes.def: Someone gets turned into a wish-granting entity.

tropes.name: Becoming the Mask
tropes.def: A character becomes like the person they pretend to be.

tropes.name: Belated Happy Ending
tropes.def: A story with an Ambiguous Ending is given a happy ending in the sequel.

tropes.name: Benched Hero
tropes.def: A hero is temporarily removed to keep things interesting.

tropes.name: Benevolent Conspiracy
tropes.def: A secret plan is happening, but for noble reasons.

tropes.name: Better as Friends
tropes.def: The pair decide they're happier when they're not a couple.

tropes.name: "Better If Not Born" Plot
tropes.def: Someone is shown what the world would be like if they never existed, and everyone's lives are enriched because of it.

tropes.name: Big Damn Heroes
tropes.def: The heroes pull off a dramatic rescue.

tropes.name: Big First Choice
tropes.def: An early decision has massive impact on the entire rest of the story.

tropes.name: Birthday Beginning
tropes.def: The story begins with the announcement that it's the main character's birthday, and often it's the day they reach adulthood.

tropes.name: Birthday Party Goes Wrong
tropes.def: A birthday party is getting ruined: the cake is burnt or dropped, the presents are horrible, the guests are annoying... and the birthday kid ends up unhappy on their special day. Unless his family and friends try to make it up for them and cheer them up.

tropes.name: Bittersweet 17
tropes.def: A 17-year-old who is in their coming-of-age.

tropes.name: Black Like Me
tropes.def: A character disguises themself as a member of a different social group and discovers how they are treated differently.

tropes.name: Blithe Spirit
tropes.def: An unusual stranger who goes to a straight-laced land and teaches others to think differently about themselves.

tropes.name: Blitz Evacuees
tropes.def: A child protagonist is evacuated from a city under attack and is sent to live in the country.

tropes.name: Blood Transfusion Plot
tropes.def: A character needs a blood transfusion, but there are complications.

tropes.name: Bloodbath Villain Origin
tropes.def: A villain's Start of Darkness is them committing a mass murder.

tropes.name: Bluffing the Murderer
tropes.def: Somebody is pretty sure who dunnit, but doesn't know for sure so tries to trick the suspect into confessing.

tropes.name: Body-Count Competition
tropes.def: Characters compete to see who kills the most Mooks .

tropes.name: Body Horror
tropes.def: A plot involving grotesque body structures.

tropes.name: Body Snatcher
tropes.def: A character's body is taken over by some foreign intelligence.

tropes.name: Body Surf
tropes.def: A character possesses multiple people in succession.

tropes.name: Bolivian Army Ending
tropes.def: The work ends on a cliffhanger, with the characters facing Uncertain Doom .

tropes.name: Bonfire Dance
tropes.def: (if romantic)

tropes.name: Booked Full of Mooks
tropes.def: A character in a public space discovers that all the bystanders around them are actually another character's employees or co-conspirators.

tropes.name: Bookends
tropes.def: The beginning and ending of a story occur under similar circumstances and are tied together somehow.

tropes.name: Boring Return Journey
tropes.def: The trip back home pales in comparison to the adventure it took to get to the destination.

tropes.name: Boy Meets Girl
tropes.def: A boy and a girl meet each other, lose each other, then find each other again.

tropes.name: Brainwashed
tropes.def: Someone has used Applied Phlebotinum to control the mind of another character.

tropes.name: Brainwashed and Crazy
tropes.def: A brainwashed character is sent to hurt or kill their friends.

tropes.name: "Brave the Ride" Plot
tropes.def: An episode set at an amusement park where a character must get over their fear of a ride, usually a roller coaster.

tropes.name: Breaking Out the Boss
tropes.def: Members of a gang of criminals orchestrate a plan to free their incarcerated leader from prison.

tropes.name: Bring Help Back
tropes.def: A group in distress sends one of their own to get help for them.

tropes.name: Bring It Back Alive
tropes.def: A character must capture a dangerous creature alive.

tropes.name: Bring News Back
tropes.def: The characters must get information to the right people.

tropes.name: Broken Masquerade
tropes.def: Someone discovers the truth behind a Masquerade .

tropes.name: Broken Pedestal
tropes.def: A person who idolized someone they saw as a hero starts hating their hero after discovering them to not truly be the flawless paragon of virtue they thought they were.

tropes.name: Broken Treasure
tropes.def: A character's most prized possession is broken while they are away, and now the other characters have to fix it or replace it before the character gets back.

tropes.name: Broken Win/Loss Streak
tropes.def: A streak of consecutive wins or losses is broken.

tropes.name: Brought Down to Badass
tropes.def: A super-powered being loses their powers, but is still plenty strong and formidable without powers.

tropes.name: Brought Down to Normal
tropes.def: A character with powers loses or is stripped of them, and must cope without them and/or get them back.

tropes.name: Bruce Wayne Held Hostage
tropes.def: A Superhero in their Secret Identity is taken hostage and has to save the day without blowing their cover.

tropes.name: Bucket List
tropes.def: To do everything on a certain list before one dies.

tropes.name: Bury Me Not on the Lone Prairie
tropes.def: Someone has difficulty honoring the last requests of a deceased person.

tropes.name: But I Can't Be Pregnant!
tropes.def: A character turns out to be pregnant, despite this being thought impossible.

tropes.name: But Now I Must Go
tropes.def: A work or installment of a work ends with a character who helped having to leave for no other reason than "it's the way things need to go".

tropes.name: Cabin Fever
tropes.def: Characters go crazy from being cooped up in an isolated area for an extended period with no outside contact.

tropes.name: Cain and Abel
tropes.def: Sibling rivalry turns into bitter, murderous hatred.

tropes.name: Call of the Wild Blue Yonder
tropes.def: Pure wanderlust.

tropes.name: Call Reception Area
tropes.def: Unless you want to go on an adventure, don't go here.

tropes.name: Call to Agriculture
tropes.def: A badass/heroic character retires as a farmer.

tropes.name: Came Back with a Vengeance
tropes.def: A wronged innocent returns under an assumed name in order to take revenge on their former tormentors. Inspired by The Count of Monte Cristo .

tropes.name: Cannot Spit It Out
tropes.def: One character tries to confess their love, but can't bring themself to say it. I "Uh" You, Too : ...but other gets the message regardless.

tropes.name: Can't Get Away with Nuthin'
tropes.def: Do something bad? Even once? You're gonna get it, pal.

tropes.name: Can't Get in Trouble for Nuthin'
tropes.def: A character wants to get in trouble, but can't.

tropes.name: Can't Live With Them, Can't Live Without Them
Can't Refuse the Call Anymore
tropes.def: The Chosen One can no longer ignore their destiny.

tropes.name: Can't Stop the Signal
tropes.def: The discoverers of a hidden secret, attempt to ensure it's spread far and wide.

tropes.name: Caper Rationalization
tropes.def: The group of people doing The Caper have a good reason to steal.

tropes.name: Captured Super-Entity
tropes.def: Experimenting on captive aliens.

tropes.name: Cattle Drive
tropes.def: An old Western plot involving ranchers having to get cattle to market under dangerous conditions.

tropes.name: Caught in the Bad Part of Town
tropes.def: A character finds themselves in an unfamiliar and run down (and often dangerous) neighborhood.

tropes.name: Caught Up in a Robbery
tropes.def: A plot in which a work's main or supporting characters get wrapped up in a robbery that suddenly and unexpectedly occurs at their location.

tropes.name: Celebrity is Overrated
tropes.def: Fame isn't all it's cracked up to be.

tropes.name: Celebrity Lie
tropes.def: Lying about being close to a celebrity.

tropes.name: Chain of Deals
tropes.def: Someone has to make deals with a whole bunch of people in order to get what they want.

tropes.name: Chained Heat
tropes.def: Characters become literally attached to each other and must work together in order to reverse it.

tropes.name: Champions on the Inside
tropes.def: The characters lose the championship, but still feel like winners on the inside.

tropes.name: Changeling Fantasy
tropes.def: A character's real parents are much more exciting than their other ones.

tropes.name: Changing of the Guard
tropes.def: A sequel which features or focuses on different characters from the original work.

tropes.name: Chased by Angry Natives
tropes.def: A character gets chased by angry native population.

tropes.name: Chased Off into the Sunset
tropes.def: The story ends with a character being chased by another character towards the sunset.

tropes.name: Children Raise You
tropes.def: Character Development comes from looking after a kid.

tropes.name: Cinderella Plot
tropes.def: Plots inspired by or parodying Cinderella .

tropes.name: Clean Up the Town
tropes.def: A new person comes to a rundown town, intending to reduce crime and make it a better place.

tropes.name: Clear My Name
tropes.def: Someone has to prove they're innocent of the crime they're accused of committing.

tropes.name: Clear Their Name
tropes.def: Someone else takes it upon them to prove the innocence of someone wrongly accused of a crime.

tropes.name: Climactic Maiming
tropes.def: A character suffers a major injury or disfigurement during the climax of the story.

tropes.name: Closed Circle
tropes.def: No way to get out. No way to get help. You're on your own.

tropes.name: Code Silver
tropes.def: A gunman takes hostages at a hospital, school, or other important place where the characters work.

tropes.name: Cold Equation
tropes.def: In a survival situation, can killing one to save others be a solution?

tropes.name: Color Me Black
tropes.def: A character is turned into a member of another race in order to teach them a lesson about racism.

tropes.name: Coming of Age Story
tropes.def: A child or adolescent learns to be more mature.

tropes.name: Community-Threatening Construction
tropes.def: A planned construction site motivates residents to defend their home, which is subject for demolition.

tropes.name: Compromising Memoirs
tropes.def: A memoir is written that contains details about a person that the person does not wish others to know.

tropes.name: Conclusive Confession
tropes.def: A culprit is confronted with evidence of something they did, in turn pushing them to confess and try to justify their actions or provide motives.

tropes.name: Consequence Combo
tropes.def: The Call comes. If the Chosen One says "yes", they get a prize. If they say "no", something horrible will happen.

tropes.name: Consolation World Record
tropes.def: Someone fails to break a record and gain recognition for it, but in doing so ends up unintentionally breaking a world record anyway.

tropes.name: Contamination Situation
tropes.def: Characters are exposed to a potentially deadly pathogen that infects them.

tropes.name: Contract on the Hitman
tropes.def: An assassin is marked for death by the very people for whom they work.

tropes.name: Cooking Duel
tropes.def: Two rivals compete over who can make better food.

tropes.name: Cooperation Gambit
tropes.def: Two enemies make a deal with each other without ending their conflict.

tropes.name: Cosmetic Catastrophe
tropes.def: A girl experiments with makeup for the first time, with negative consequences.

tropes.name: Cosmic Horror Reveal
tropes.def: A story ends with revealing it's actually a Cosmic Horror Story .

tropes.name: Counter Zany
tropes.def: A Zany Scheme is countered by an even Zanier Scheme.

tropes.name: Couple's Retreat Plot
tropes.def: A couple or group of couples go on a vacation/getaway/holiday to enjoy themselves or repair/save their marriage.

tropes.name: Courtroom Episode
tropes.def: An episode revolves around someone being put on trial for their transgressions.

tropes.name: Crapsack World
tropes.def: The story takes place in a terrible location to live.

tropes.name: Crash Course Landing
tropes.def: A character with no flying experience has to learn how to land a plane safely.

tropes.name: Crashing the Coronation
tropes.def: A mission to stop the wrong person from being crowned ruler.

tropes.name: Credit Card Plot
tropes.def: A character gets a credit card and starts spending it irresponsibly.

tropes.name: Crossing the Desert
tropes.def: The hero must cross a desert.

tropes.name: Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass
tropes.def: An idiot who can become awesome in situations.

tropes.name: Crying Wolf
tropes.def: Pull too many deliberate false alarms and no one will believe you when you're trying to warn about real danger.

tropes.name: Cryptid Episode
tropes.def: The characters go and search for some kind of mysterious mythical creature.

tropes.name: Cuckoo Nest
tropes.def: A character is convinced they're in an asylum and the events of the work were just hallucinations, making it (sometimes temporarily, sometimes permanently) ambiguous as to what's real.

tropes.name: Cultural Personality Makeover
tropes.def: A character discovers something: a photo, a family record, etc., that reveals some long-lost ancestor or unknown relative belonged to some particular unusual culture.

tropes.name: Curtain Call
tropes.def: The whole cast comes out at the end of the story.

tropes.name: Cutting the Knot
tropes.def: Solving or bypassing a puzzle with brute force.

tropes.name: Dance Party Ending
tropes.def: The story ends with everyone dancing.

tropes.name: Danger with a Deadline
tropes.def: An enemy or obstacle is extremely dangerous, but only for a finite period of time. The plot comes from surviving or avoiding this danger.

tropes.name: Dangerous Device Disposal Debacle
tropes.def: Because someone didn't dispose of a Plot Device correctly, it can be freely utilized again for more plot.

tropes.name: Darkened Building Shootout
tropes.def: A classic denouement — the hero and villain have a shootout in a darkened building, with a suitably suspenseful final shot.

tropes.name: Dawn of an Era
tropes.def: The story ends with the start of a new era.

tropes.name: Dead Alternate Counterpart
tropes.def: Character visits an alternate reality where their counterpart has died.

tropes.name: Dead Pet Sketch
tropes.def: Someone has to take care of someone else's pet while the someone else is away. The pet ends up dying.

tropes.name: Deadly Distant Finale
tropes.def: The story ends with a flash forward to a character's later years where they die.

tropes.name: Deadly Game
tropes.def: When the consequences of losing the game is death.

tropes.name: Deadly Graduation
tropes.def: A character in an evil training program must battle their friend to the death as a final test.

tropes.name: Deadly Road Trip
tropes.def: Ending up in peril while on vacation.

tropes.name: Deadly Upgrade
tropes.def: Character gets an enormous power boost, at the eventual cost of his/her life.

tropes.name: Deal with the Devil
tropes.def: A crooked bargain with an evil person or entity for something one wants, with a bad price attached.

tropes.name: Death by Flashback
tropes.def: Revealing a character's backstory is a good indication that they are about to die.

tropes.name: Death Is a Sad Thing
tropes.def: Children learn about death for the first time and are saddened by it.

tropes.name: Death of the Hypotenuse
tropes.def: The third person in a Love Triangle passes away, thus solving the issue in question for the other two characters.

tropes.name: Death Takes a Holiday
tropes.def: For some reason, The Grim Reaper stops making people die.

tropes.name: Declaration of Personal Independence
tropes.def: Someone attempts to strike out on their own against their guardians' wishes.

tropes.name: Defeat by Transformation
tropes.def: In the end, the villain can only be defeated by being transformed.

tropes.name: Defeat Means Menial Labor
tropes.def: Where the villain, upon defeat, is reduced to performing menial labor.

tropes.name: Defeating the Cheating Opponent
tropes.def: The protagonist must beat their opponent fairly after the opponent has been caught cheating.

tropes.name: Defector from Commie Land
tropes.def: A character is in need of escape from a land where a dictatorial regime is ruling.

tropes.name: Delayed Family Acceptance
tropes.def: It's difficult for a character's family member(s) to come to terms with a revelation about that character.

tropes.name: Demorphing Denouement
tropes.def: The story's climax or ending features a transformed character being restored to their original form.

tropes.name: Dénouement
tropes.def: The story ends with loose ends being tied up after The Climax .

tropes.name: Dénouement Episode
tropes.def: The final episode is an epilogue to the Grand Finale .

tropes.name: De-power
tropes.def: A superpowered character loses their powers.

tropes.name: Descent into Addiction
tropes.def: A character gets involved with drugs or some other substance or experience and descends into addiction.

tropes.name: Deserted Island
tropes.def: A small island that's completely uninhabited.

tropes.name: Desperately Looking for a Purpose in Life
tropes.def: The Chosen One is desperate for a cause to fight for.

tropes.name: Despite the Plan
tropes.def: The plan goes horribly wrong, but the heroes achieve their goal anyway.

tropes.name: Destroy the Evidence
tropes.def: Someone who seems not to be directly involved in a crime destroys or hides some evidence relating to it.

tropes.name: Destructive Saviour
tropes.def: When a hero causes massive destruction in the course of trying to save a place from a bad guy.

tropes.name: Deus ex Machina
tropes.def: An event from out of nowhere causes things to shift to the hero's favor.

tropes.name: Diabolus ex Machina
tropes.def: A plot device that gets the heroes into danger.

tropes.name: "Die Hard" on an X
tropes.def: Bad guys have taken over a place and taken everyone hostage. The hero is in the place, and must save the day by kicking the bad guys' asses.

tropes.name: Digging to China
tropes.def: Someone tries to go to China by digging deep enough into the Earth.

tropes.name: Dinner with the Boss
tropes.def: A character's boss comes to their home for dinner.

tropes.name: Disney Death
tropes.def: A character who appeared to die at first subsequently turns out to still be alive or is miraculously resurrected.

tropes.name: Disney Villain Death
tropes.def: The villain ends up falling to their death.

tropes.name: Distant Finale
tropes.def: The story ends after a Time Skip with the characters much older.

tropes.name: Distant Prologue
tropes.def: A short introduction scene at the start of the story that takes place a long time before the main plot happens.

tropes.name: Divide and Conquer
tropes.def: When a villain gets his enemies fighting each other instead of him.

tropes.name: Divided We Fall
tropes.def: Dissension between the heroes gets in the way stopping the villain.

tropes.name: Doctor Infected by Patient
tropes.def: A doctor treating a sick patient catches what the patient has.

tropes.name: Don't Celebrate Just Yet
tropes.def: The heroes defeat a villain but realize they still have to take care of something else that's occurring.

tropes.name: Don't Go in the Woods
tropes.def: Terrible things happen to those who wander into the forest.

tropes.name: Doomed Hometown
tropes.def: The destruction of the hero's hometown is what stirs them into the adventure.

tropes.name: Doomed Moral Victor
tropes.def: The Hero dies after making his Last Stand .

tropes.name: Doomed Rebellion
tropes.def: A story about a character going against society ends with society getting the last laugh.

tropes.name: Doorstop Baby
tropes.def: A baby left on someone's doorstep gets adopted by whomever lives in the house.

tropes.name: Dork Horse Candidate
tropes.def: An underdog character competes against a more popular opponent in an election.

tropes.name: Down the Rabbit Hole
tropes.def: A character travels to a bizarro world in a plot structure of Alice in Wonderland .

tropes.name: Downer Beginning
tropes.def: The story begins tragically.

tropes.name: Downer Ending
tropes.def: The story ends on a tragic note.

tropes.name: Drama Bomb Finale
tropes.def: An otherwise comedic story trying its hand at a dramatic moment near the show's last episode or two, totally out of left field.

tropes.name: Dramatic Chase Opening
tropes.def: The story begins with a dramatic chase scene.

tropes.name: Dreaded Kids' Table
tropes.def: An older child longs to sit with the adults instead of the kids during a family meal.

tropes.name: Dream Intro
tropes.def: The story begins with a character's dream sequence.

tropes.name: Driving Question
tropes.def: The core element of a plot is a mystery.

tropes.name: Duel to the Death
tropes.def: Two characters, rivals or enemies, go mano a mano , and only one will survive. Usually.

tropes.name: Duels Decide Everything
tropes.def: All major conflicts in a work are settled by fair, one-on-one contests.

tropes.name: Dying Declaration of Love
tropes.def: ...moments before dying.

tropes.name: Ear-Piercing Plot
tropes.def: A young character wants their ears pierced, but is either too scared to do it or is forbidden from doing so by their parents.

tropes.name: Earn Your Happy Ending
tropes.def: The character doesn't get their happy ending until after enduring a lot of suffering.

tropes.name: Easing into the Adventure
tropes.def: A prologue that covers the protagonist's ordinary life before going on the adventure.

tropes.name: Election Day Episode
tropes.def: Two or more characters run for an elective office.

tropes.name: Embarrassing Rescue
tropes.def: A character finds being rescued embarrassing and is angry with the rescuer for helping them.

tropes.name: Emergency Impersonation
tropes.def: A character who recently died or has been incapacitated is needed for something, so some other character has to impersonate and fill in for them.

tropes.name: Empty Quiver
tropes.def: A nuke or other weapon of mass destruction has gone missing, and now the race is on to retrieve it before it falls into the wrong hands.

tropes.name: End of an Age
tropes.def: The story is set during the end of a particular era in the story's setting, such as the end of the medieval era or the end of the American West.

tropes.name: "End of the World" Special
tropes.def: A character is given the power to recreate the whole world.

tropes.name: Ends with a Smile
tropes.def: Any story (whether an episode or a full-scale work) ends with a character or characters smiling.

tropes.name: Endurance Duel
tropes.def: A showdown to see who can last the longest doing dangerous activities.

tropes.name: Enemy Mine
tropes.def: The hero and the villain reluctantly join forces to defeat a mutual enemy.

tropes.name: Engineered Public Confession
tropes.def: A villain who has been able to hide their true nature from the public is tricked by the heroes into publicly admitting that they are a horrible person who was deceiving everyone.

tropes.name: Enthusiastic Newbie Teacher
tropes.def: A friendly teacher who is just out of schooling.

tropes.name: Entry Point
tropes.def: The player's way into an Alternate Reality Game .

tropes.name: Epic Race
tropes.def: The characters have to proceed from a starting line to a finishing line under some set of rules over the course of an extended period of time.

tropes.name: Epilogue Letter
tropes.def: A series ends with the narration of a letter.

tropes.name: Epiphanic Prison
tropes.def: A prison someone can't escape from unless they have an epiphany.

tropes.name: Equalizing the Interspecies Romance
tropes.def: The story ends with one of the characters in an Interspecies Relationship becoming the other's species.

tropes.name: Equivalent Exchange
tropes.def: Giving up something that is equal to what a character desires.

tropes.name: Escape from the Crazy Place
tropes.def: A character is trapped in a horror setting from which they must escape.

tropes.name: Establishing Character Moment
tropes.def: The first thing a character says or does that makes it clear the kind of person they are.

tropes.name: "Eureka!" Moment
tropes.def: A character's thoughts or observations inspire them to come up with a plan.

tropes.name: Everybody Did It
tropes.def: The mystery ends with every suspect guilty.

tropes.name: "Everybody Helps Out" Denouement
tropes.def: The story ends with all the characters coming together to help people out.

tropes.name: Everybody Lives
tropes.def: The story ends with no one dying.

tropes.name: Everybody Must Get Stoned
tropes.def: Most or all of the cast gets exposed to some kind of substance that alters their behavior.

tropes.name: Everybody's Dead, Dave
tropes.def: A work where all but one character is dead.

tropes.name: Everyone Join the Party
tropes.def: Random people join the hero or the villain for the final battle.

tropes.name: Everyone Meets Everyone
tropes.def: The first episode shows the main cast coming together.

tropes.name: Everything but the Girl
tropes.def: A character can achieve or gain everything they want with the exception of their love interest's affections.

tropes.name: Evil Plan
tropes.def: The villain's plan to do something evil.

tropes.name: Evil Twin
tropes.def: A character has a twin who is evil.

tropes.name: Evil Will Fail
tropes.def: The Big Bad loses not just because the heroes were stronger, but because it is inherent to nature that evil will fail.

tropes.name: Eviler than Thou
tropes.def: A villain proves they're more evil than another villain.

tropes.name: Exact Words
tropes.def: It's revealed that what a person said was intended in the exact phrasing and wasn't an idiom or figure of speech.

tropes.name: Excuse Plot
tropes.def: A plot that's just an excuse for the action happening.

tropes.name: Exit, Pursued by a Bear
tropes.def: The story ends with the villain being chased by a creature that intends to harm them.

tropes.name: Experimental Archeology
tropes.def: A character tries to prove that an ancient voyage actually occurred by doing it themselves.

tropes.name: Extreme Sports Plot
tropes.def: A show or movie that has the characters doing extreme sports.

tropes.name: Fabula and Sujet
tropes.def: Distinction between the chronological order of the story's events (Fabula) and the order in which we see the scenes (Sujet).

tropes.name: Failed Audition Plot
tropes.def: A character fails their audition but learns to move forward and not give up.

tropes.name: Failure Gambit
tropes.def: Failing intentionally as part of a grander scheme.

tropes.name: Fairest of Them All
tropes.def: A villain who will not stand for anyone being more beautiful than they are.

tropes.name: Fake Action Prologue
tropes.def: The story starts out with what appears to be an action scene, but it turns out to be fake.

tropes.name: Fake Mystery
tropes.def: The crime turns out to be staged/faked.

tropes.name: Fake-Out Twist
tropes.def: There are two ending plot reveals, the second of which changes the meaning of the first.

tropes.name: Fake Relationship
tropes.def: Two characters who aren't romantically interested in each other pretend to be a couple.

tropes.name: Faked Rip Van Winkle
tropes.def: Someone is tricked into thinking that they've woken up in the future.

tropes.name: Fall-in Angel
tropes.def: A girl falling from the sky is what kickstarts the plot.

tropes.name: Falling into the Plot
tropes.def: The protagonist falls from the sky at the start of a work.

tropes.name: False Crucible
tropes.def: A character is put through a grueling test that turns out to be fake.

tropes.name: False Utopia
tropes.def: A "utopian" setting that turns out to be anything but, usually with a horrible secret involved.

tropes.name: Familial Fame Frustrations
tropes.def: When a family member or members are negatively impacted as a direct result of one or more of their relatives being famous and they have to figure out how to deal with that.

tropes.name: Family Disunion
tropes.def: Family reunions are a source of major drama.

tropes.name: Family Relationship Switcheroo
tropes.def: A person finds out that their relative was actually related to them in a different way than they originally believed.

tropes.name: "Fantastic Voyage" Plot
tropes.def: Curing a sick person by shrinking and entering their body to confront the germs.

tropes.name: Fantasy All Along
tropes.def: It turns out the events were all just part of someone's delusion.

tropes.name: Fantasy Keepsake
