tropes.def: Someone wakes up, thinking the whole adventure was All Just a Dream , only to find an item proving the adventure was real.

tropes.name: Fast-Forward to Reunion
tropes.def: The main plot resolves with characters going separate ways, the ending skips to future to when they eventually reunite.

tropes.name: Fatal Forced March
tropes.def: Characters are forced to make a dangerous and likely-deadly journey on foot through hostile territory.

tropes.name: Faustian Rebellion
tropes.def: Someone who made a Deal with the Devil decides to show the Devil where he can stick it. Forcefully.

tropes.name: Faux Adventure Story
tropes.def: A story promises adventure, but doesn't deliver.

tropes.name: Fauxtastic Voyage
tropes.def: Characters are promised a trip around the world, but is tricked and doesn't experience a real trip.

tropes.name: Favouritism Flip-Flop
tropes.def: Changing your opinion on something just because someone else has a different opinion.

tropes.name: "Fawlty Towers" Plot
tropes.def: A lie is told which must be propped up with more lies before everything cannot be sustained and goes crashing down.

tropes.name: Fidelity Test
tropes.def: A character tests their spouse's faithfulness to them.

tropes.name: Field Trip to the Past
tropes.def: Someone learns history by experiencing it.

tropes.name: 15 Minutes of Fame
tropes.def: Someone becomes famous for a short amount of time.

tropes.name: Fight Clubbing
tropes.def: People meet in secret to beat each other senseless.

tropes.name: Fight Dracula
tropes.def: Previously established heroes take on Count Dracula as their latest opponent.

tropes.name: Fight to Survive
tropes.def: Characters struggle to survive a perilous situation.

tropes.name: Fighting for a Homeland
tropes.def: Group of people fight for ownership of a land to claim as their home.

tropes.name: Final Boss
tropes.def: The video game ends with one last boss fight that the player must win to finish the game. The final boss will almost always be the main antagonist.

tropes.name: Final Girl
tropes.def: A female character who survives the events of the story after everyone else dies.

tropes.name: Find the Cure
tropes.def: A plot focused on finding a cure for something.

tropes.name: Finding Judas
tropes.def: A character willingly betrays the protagonists for benevolent reasons.

tropes.name: First Kiss
tropes.def: The pair finally kiss. The Big Damn Kiss

tropes.name: First Pet Story
tropes.def: A plot detailing a character adopting their first pet.

tropes.name: First Time in the Sun
tropes.def: A character who has lived in seclusion their whole life experiences sunlight the outdoors for the first time.

tropes.name: Fish out of Temporal Water
tropes.def: Someone is forced to adjust living outside of their original time period.

tropes.name: Fish Out of Water
tropes.def: A character is placed in a situation completely unfamiliar to them.

tropes.name: Fission Mailed
tropes.def: A video game pretends that it's Game Over when it really isn't.

tropes.name: Flash Forward
tropes.def: A break in the story to show a future plot development ahead of time.

tropes.name: Flashback B-Plot
tropes.def: A linear secondary story is told through flashbacks alongside the main story, both involving the same character(s).

tropes.name: Flashback... Back... Back...
tropes.def: Flashback is preceded by an echoey sound effect.

tropes.name: Flashback Cut
tropes.def: A very brief flashback (usually lasts a few seconds) in the middle of a scene

tropes.name: Flashback Echo
tropes.def: Events in the present are quickly followed by flashbacks to similar events in the past.

tropes.name: Flashback Effects
tropes.def: Visual and audio effects used to indicate a flashback.

tropes.name: Flashback Nightmare
tropes.def: A character dreams of a traumatic past event.

tropes.name: Flashback Stares
tropes.def: A character stares into the distance while remembering a past event.

tropes.name: Flashback to Catchphrase
tropes.def: A flashback reveals the origin of a character's catchphrase.

tropes.name: Flashback Twist
tropes.def: A flashback is used and subverts the audience's expectations.

tropes.name: Flashback with the Other Darrin
tropes.def: A flashback to a previously shot scene with a new actor .

tropes.name: Flashback Within a Flashback
tropes.def: A flashback occurs inside another flashback.

tropes.name: Flatline Plotline
tropes.def: Characters make it so they die for a certain amount of time.

tropes.name: Flower from the Mountaintop
tropes.def: A rare or precious flower that has to be retrieved through a difficult mountain expedition.

tropes.name: "Flowers for Algernon" Syndrome
tropes.def: The improvements you obtain will eventually be reverted, sometimes for the best.

tropes.name: Food End
tropes.def: Work ends by showing characters eating.

tropes.name: For Great Justice
tropes.def: The motive or reason is stated in the opening.

tropes.name: For Science!
tropes.def: Doing anything, no matter how unethical or bizarre, for the sake of scientific progress.

tropes.name: Forced Out of the Closet
tropes.def: People who discover or assume a character is gay and in the closet decide that the best thing to do is to publicly reveal the person's secret against their wishes.

tropes.name: Foregone Conclusion
tropes.def: The story begins by letting the audience know how it'll end.

tropes.name: Forgiveness Requires Death
tropes.def: In order to be forgiven for their crimes, the character must die.

tropes.name: Forgot the Call
tropes.def: A character gets amnesia and forgets that they're an action hero.

tropes.name: Forgotten Anniversary
tropes.def: A character forgets the anniversary of their wedding or another significant event.

tropes.name: Forgotten Framing Device
tropes.def: A story that begins with a Framing Device doesn't include it in the ending.

tropes.name: Fourth Wall Farewell
tropes.def: The final moments of a work involve a sudden breaking of the fourth wall .

tropes.name: Fourth Wall Shut-In Story
tropes.def: A creator gets trapped within their own creation.

tropes.name: Framing Device
tropes.def: A story being told in the main plot of a work. Forgotten Framing Device : The story within another story is missing the latter half of its outer frame.

tropes.name: "Freaky Friday" Flip
tropes.def: Two people get their brains switched and have to find a way to get their minds restored to the proper bodies.

tropes.name: Free the Frogs
tropes.def: Protesting against frogs being dissected in science class.

tropes.name: Frequently-Broken Unbreakable Vow
tropes.def: Someone makes The Promise or a Heroic Vow , and is forced by some circumstance or another to break it. Repeatedly.

tropes.name: Friendly Scheming
tropes.def: The protagonist finds out that everything that's been happening was all part of an elaborate scheme set up by their friends.

tropes.name: Frivolous Lawsuit
tropes.def: Someone makes a lawsuit over a ridiculously petty slight.

tropes.name: From Beyond the Fourth Wall
tropes.def: A character receives help from the author or the viewer.

tropes.name: From New York to Nowhere
tropes.def: A character moves from a big city to a small town.

tropes.name: From Nobody to Nightmare
tropes.def: An insignificant loser becomes the scariest villain alive.

tropes.name: From Zero to Hero
tropes.def: An insignificant person becomes a hero worthy of honor.

tropes.name: Full-Party Sequence
tropes.def: While not exclusive to climaxes, they most often tend to happen there.

tropes.name: Fumbling the Gauntlet
tropes.def: A character's action against another character in an unfamiliar culture is construed as a challenge to a duel, lethal or not.

tropes.name: Fundraiser Carnival
tropes.def: The characters organize a carnival to raise money for a charity or other cause.

tropes.name: Futureshadowing
tropes.def: We see the aftermath of an event before seeing the event itself.

tropes.name: Gambit Roulette
tropes.def: A convoluted plan that hinges on unpredictable factors actually succeeds.

tropes.name: Game Show Appearance
tropes.def: Characters appear on a real or fictitious game show.

tropes.name: Garage Band
tropes.def: A ragtag group of characters start their own band.

tropes.name: Garage Sale
tropes.def: To earn money, the characters sell some of their old junk in a garage sale/yard sale/etc.

tropes.name: Garrulous Growth
tropes.def: A sentient, talking protrusion that usually wants to take over the human body on which it grows.

tropes.name: Gender-Invading Sleepovers
tropes.def: Boys try to get in to a girls-only sleepover, or vice-versa.

tropes.name: "Gender-Normative Parent" Plot
tropes.def: A boy has an interest in a "girlish" hobby, and his father pushes him to follow a "manly" one.

tropes.name: Generational Saga
tropes.def: A tale spanning multiple generations of the same family.

tropes.name: Generational Trauma
tropes.def: Conflict arises due to unresolved baggage passed down from generation to generation.

tropes.name: Genocide Backfire
tropes.def: An evil tyrant or regime seeks to wipe out a people because they fear they are a threat to their power. Unfortunately for them, someone manages to survive.

tropes.name: Get Back to the Future
tropes.def: Someone is sent to the past and has to find their way back.

tropes.name: "Getting My Own Room" Plot
tropes.def: A child who has always shared a room with siblings finally gets their own room.

tropes.name: "Getting Ready for Bed" Plot
tropes.def: An episode set late at night, where a character readies themselves for sleep... Or the point is getting a restless character to sleep.

tropes.name: Getting Sick Deliberately
tropes.def: A character tries to get themselves sick so that they can get out of an obligation.

tropes.name: Ghost Ship
tropes.def: Creepy and/or haunted abandoned ships.

tropes.name: Ghost Story
tropes.def: Stories about ghosts.

tropes.name: Girls Behind Bars
tropes.def: A female character is thrown into a women's prison, which is often played for titillation.

tropes.name: Girls vs. Boys Plot
tropes.def: Boys and girls battle for supremacy.

tropes.name: Giving Radio to the Romans
tropes.def: Giving modern technology to people in the past.

tropes.name: Gladiator Revolt
tropes.def: Gladiators rebel against those that force them to fight.

tropes.name: Go Among Mad People
tropes.def: A sane person is committed to a mental institution, and needs to convince the staff that they're not crazy.

tropes.name: God and Satan Are Both Jerks
tropes.def: Neither the forces of Hell nor the forces of Heaven have anything good in mind for humanity.

tropes.name: God for a Day
tropes.def: Status as a deity proves to be too much responsibility and absolute power corrupts.

tropes.name: Godhood Seeker
tropes.def: To become a deity.

tropes.name: Going Native
tropes.def: A character adopts the customs and morality of a group which they were originally sent to infiltrate.

tropes.name: Going to See the Elephant
tropes.def: A young character travels the world to go see something new and exotic, often learning life lessons along the way.

tropes.name: Gold Fever
tropes.def: A group of characters fall prey to greed and turn on each other while on the hunt for gold or some other fabulous treasure.

tropes.name: Gondor Calls for Aid
tropes.def: The hero prepares for an epic battle by recruiting every friend, ally, enemy, and so on who is willing to help them in the fight.

tropes.name: Good All Along
tropes.def: Someone thought to be evil turns out to be good.

tropes.name: Good Morning, Crono
tropes.def: The story begins with the main character being woken up.

tropes.name: Got the Call on Speed Dial
tropes.def: The Chosen One had already finished their mission and is now looking for a new one.

tropes.name: Gotta Catch 'Em All
tropes.def: A character wants to pursue a collection.

tropes.name: Gotta Catch Them All
tropes.def: To collect everything in a set.

tropes.name: Gotta Have It, Gonna Steal It
tropes.def: Someone wants something trendy but isn't allowed/can't afford it, so they steal (or attempt to steal) it.

tropes.name: Gotta Kill Them All
tropes.def: A character wants to kill everyone on their list.

tropes.name: Government Conspiracy
tropes.def: A secret project run by a government organization, such as the military or an intelligence agency.

tropes.name: Graduate from the Story
tropes.def: The main cast of a school-centered story graduate at the ending.

tropes.name: Graduation for Everyone
tropes.def: The whole cast of a show graduate school whether they were a good student or not.

tropes.name: Grand Theft Me
tropes.def: Taking control of someone's body to make them do bad things.

tropes.name: Grass Is Greener
tropes.def: A character who longs to leave their terrible life behind to go somewhere they think is better.

tropes.name: Great Escape
tropes.def: Someone has been thrown in prison, and must now make good their escape.

tropes.name: Guarding the Portal
tropes.def: Heroes guard a dimensional portal to make sure nothing goes in or out.

tropes.name: Guess Who I'm Marrying?
tropes.def: A character's single parent has found someone. Unfortunately, that someone is anything but good for the character, and now they need to stop this!

tropes.name: Guilty Until Someone Else Is Guilty
tropes.def: A suspect can only be proven innocent by finding the true culprit.

tropes.name: Handcuffed Briefcase
tropes.def: A briefcase is holding something so important, the person holding it has it handcuffed to their wrist.

tropes.name: Happy-Ending Massage
tropes.def: A massage session turns into something quite a lot steamier than that.

tropes.name: Harbinger of Impending Doom
tropes.def: A character tries to warn everyone about something from which they barely escaped, but they just dither until it shows up anyway.

tropes.name: Hastily Hidden MacGuffin
tropes.def: A valuable stolen object, hidden to avoid detection by the authorities (or rival thieves, or whichever party is trying to take it), which the thieves then must scramble to get back.

tropes.name: Have You Tried Not Being a Monster?
tropes.def: The familial rejection in this one is supposed to be well-meaning (assuming the family loves the queer person), but it carries the implication that the queer person can and should change.

tropes.name: He Knows Too Much
tropes.def: Killing someone for getting even a smidgen close to discovering a secret they can't be allowed to know.

tropes.name: Headbutting Heroes
tropes.def: Two heroes who are anything but on the best of terms with each other.

tropes.name: The Shapeshifter
tropes.def: Someone you don't trust but nonetheless need for their capabilities or knowledge.

tropes.name: Hell Invades Heaven
tropes.def: The Legions of Hell invade Heaven itself.

tropes.name: Hell on Earth
tropes.def: The Legions of Hell invade the mortal realm.

tropes.name: Her Heart Will Go On
tropes.def: (exit point) Someone to Remember Him By

tropes.name: Heroic Rematch
tropes.def: After being defeated the first time, the hero is ready for Round Two against the villain.

tropes.name: Hero's Evil Predecessor
tropes.def: Someone had the hero's mantle or powers before them, but they have since gone evil, and now the hero now has to deal with them.

tropes.name: Hero's First Rescue
tropes.def: You saved this guy? You just heeded the call.

tropes.name: The Goddess
tropes.def: a figure that serves as inspiration to the hero, often a love interest and/or another heroic figure they admire.

tropes.name: Hired to Hunt Yourself
tropes.def: A person sent to hunt down The Mole actually is The Mole.

tropes.name: His Story Repeats Itself
tropes.def: To resolve or come to closure with something that happened in their backstory, a character experiences an event very similar to what happened before.

tropes.name: Home Sweet Home
tropes.def: A character settles down at home after a long adventure.

tropes.name: Hourglass Plot
tropes.def: Two characters on opposite ends of the moral or at least conflict spectrum change roles over the course, but are still opposed to each other.

tropes.name: House Fire
tropes.def: A plot revolves around a character's house getting damaged/destroyed in a fire and dealing with the aftermath.

tropes.name: How Dad Met Mom
tropes.def: The story of how a character's parents met each other and fell in love.

tropes.name: Humanity on Trial
tropes.def: An alien or supernatural race decides to put the human race on trial, with our continued existence on the line.

tropes.name: Humiliation Conga
tropes.def: The ending has the villain get his comeuppance by being subjected to a string of embarrassing misfortunes.

tropes.name: Hunting the Rogue
tropes.def: A rogue agent deserts from an organization they served and they're chased as a result.

tropes.name: Hurrying Home for the Holidays
tropes.def: A character needs to get somewhere in time to celebrate a holiday.

tropes.name: Hybrid All Along
tropes.def: Someone discovers that they’re a hybrid of multiple species.

tropes.name: Hybridization Plot
tropes.def: A large portion of the plot, or a character's motivation, focuses around creating a hybrid.

tropes.name: Hypno Fool
tropes.def: A person is hypnotized and Hilarity Ensues before it can be undone.

tropes.name: I Am Not Your Father
tropes.def: A father reveals to his child that they were adopted.

tropes.name: I Am Who?
tropes.def: The protagonist discovers their heroic destiny which had been kept secret from them.

tropes.name: I Choose to Stay
tropes.def: A character has the chance to go home, but decides to stay where they are now instead.

tropes.name: I Don't Want to Ruin Our Friendship
I Have Your Girlfriend
tropes.def: Cock Fight

tropes.name: I Made Copies
tropes.def: A character tears up a contract only to be told copies were made.

tropes.name: I Want My Beloved to Be Happy
I Will Find You
tropes.def: A character is searching for a loved one who has been kidnapped or has otherwise gone missing.

tropes.name: I Wish It Were Real
tropes.def: Character's favorite toy/video game/show becomes real.

tropes.name: Identity Impersonator
tropes.def: A superhero protects their secret identity by appearing in public with someone pretending to be their alter ego.

tropes.name: Ignorant of the Call
tropes.def: Everyone knows that the Chosen One is The Hero except of the Chosen One.

tropes.name: I'm Dying, Please Take My MacGuffin
tropes.def: The call starts when a dying person gives you a Plot Device .

tropes.name: Immortality Seeker
tropes.def: To live forever.

tropes.name: In Another Man's Shoes
tropes.def: Characters are forced to experience life through another's perspective.

tropes.name: In Love with the Mark
tropes.def: One character is a hired killer, and the other is the person they're supposed to kill.

tropes.name: Inciting Incident
tropes.def: An event that sets the plot in motion.

tropes.name: Indy Ploy
tropes.def: Rather than having a plan ready, the hero makes up a scheme as they go along.

tropes.name: Infinite Illusion Ending
tropes.def: The story ends with the characters in a dreamworld, unable or unwilling to awake

tropes.name: Innocence Lost
tropes.def: An innocent character is exposed to true evil, or the uglier side of the world, for the first time.

tropes.name: Insanity Establishment Scene
tropes.def: When a character is revealed to be crazy later instead of from the start.

tropes.name: Inside a Computer System
tropes.def: Characters go inside a virtual world contained within a computer.

tropes.name: Intergenerational Friendship
tropes.def: Friendship between two people who have a significant age gap.

tropes.name: Internal Reveal
tropes.def: The Reveal in-universe.

tropes.name: Intrepid Fictioneer
tropes.def: Characters breach internal fourth walls to go on adventures in books, films, etc.

tropes.name: Invented Individual
tropes.def: Somebody makes up an imaginary person and eventually has to give up the made-up person by "killing" them.

tropes.name: Invisible Main Character
tropes.def: A story where the main character temporarily becomes invisible.

tropes.name: Involuntary Charity Donation
tropes.def: Stealing from a villain and donating it to charity.

tropes.name: It Began with a Twist of Fate
tropes.def: The protagonist's involvement in a story's events results from a simple decision.

tropes.name: It Was with You All Along
It's a Wonderful Plot
tropes.def: Someone is shown what the world would be like if they never existed.

tropes.name: It's Not You, It's My Enemies
It's Personal
tropes.def: Something bad has happened to a loved one, and now the hero wants the villain responsible taken down more than ever!

tropes.name: Jackie Robinson Story
tropes.def: Someone tries to be the first of their race or sex in a field occupied solely by white males.

tropes.name: "Jaws" Attack Parody
tropes.def: A shark (or any other dangerous creature) threatens a small-town community, parodying the film Jaws 1 .

tropes.name: Jekyll & Hyde
tropes.def: A good person who transforms into a villainous alter ego.

tropes.name: Jigsaw Puzzle Plot
tropes.def: A plot that's fed to the audience a little bit at a time.

tropes.name: Journey of Reclamation
tropes.def: A character seeks to regain something they lost.

tropes.name: Journey to the Center of the Mind
tropes.def: A character enters the physical manifestation of someone's mind.

tropes.name: Judgment of Solomon
tropes.def: Two people claim to be the true owner of something, and the judge chooses to split it to decide the true owner.

tropes.name: Jumped at the Call
tropes.def: The Chosen One gets the call and can't wait to heed it.

tropes.name: Jumping Off the Slippery Slope
tropes.def: A character goes evil very quickly after doing some warned-against but otherwise innocuous thing.

tropes.name: Just Friends
tropes.def: The pair aren't officially a couple yet. Attractiveness Isolation

tropes.name: Just Think of the Potential!
tropes.def: A character has a vision for the future and tries to share their vision with others.

tropes.name: Kafka Komedy
tropes.def: A story where the character's misfortune and misery are played for Black Comedy .

tropes.name: Kansas City Shuffle
tropes.def: A con where the mark figures out an obvious scam only to fall right into a different one.

tropes.name: Kidnapped by the Call
tropes.def: The Call gives the Chosen One no choice in heeding it.

tropes.name: Kids Play Matchmaker
tropes.def: The children of single parents decide to try to get their parents together.

tropes.name: Kill Me Now, or Forever Stay Your Hand
tropes.def: The hero offers their antagonist a chance to kill them, knowing the other person isn't so far gone as to commit murder.

tropes.name: Killed to Uphold the Masquerade
tropes.def: Someone is killed to prevent them from exposing the existence of supernatural beings.

tropes.name: Last Day of Normalcy
tropes.def: The audience is shown the heroes in their home setting before their normal lives are changed forever

tropes.name: Last Fertile Region
tropes.def: The last place to support life in an otherwise barren world.

tropes.name: Last Moment Together
tropes.def: Two people (friends, family, or lovers) are together for what they know is the final time.

tropes.name: Last Stand
tropes.def: Someone kills as many enemies as they can before they die.

tropes.name: Last Villain Stand
tropes.def: The villain makes a final attempt to beat the heroes.

tropes.name: Late to the Tragedy
tropes.def: Something bad has happened in the location, and the character arrives too late to prevent it.

tropes.name: "Leave Your Quest" Test
tropes.def: The hero is tested by being tempted into abandoning their mission.

tropes.name: Leaving You to Find Myself
tropes.def: A character is changing intellectually and dumps their partner to live a new life.

tropes.name: Led by the Outsider
tropes.def: The hero becomes a leader of another group.

tropes.name: Legion of Doom
tropes.def: Several of the hero's enemies team up in a plot to have their revenge against the hero.

tropes.name: Let the Past Burn
tropes.def: The story ends with a fire destroying the house, along with all it represents.

tropes.name: Like a Duck Takes to Water
tropes.def: A character has knowledge that makes them able to adapt to another time/world.

tropes.name: Like You Were Dying
tropes.def: A character radically changes their behavior because they're dying.

tropes.name: Literal Transformative Experience
tropes.def: A character undergoes a drastic transformation and sees their personality change as a result of their experiences.

tropes.name: Lonely at the Top
tropes.def: A character gets everything they want, but loses everything and everyone they loved in the process.

tropes.name: Long Game
tropes.def: A master plan that takes a long time to complete.

tropes.name: Lost Orphaned Royalty
tropes.def: An orphan turns out to be descended from royalty.

tropes.name: Lottery of Doom
tropes.def: A lottery or other game that you really, really don't want to win.

tropes.name: Lotus-Eater Machine
tropes.def: Someone is trapped in a dream-like fantasy where everything's the way it should be to make the person happy and content.

tropes.name: Love at First Sight
tropes.def: One or both characters fall in love the moment they see the other.

tropes.name: Love Before First Sight
tropes.def: One or both characters fall in love with their love interest before they even meet. Because Destiny Says So

tropes.name: Love Confession
tropes.def: One character confesses their love for the other. Accidental Declaration of Love : ...unintentionally.

tropes.name: Love Confessor
tropes.def: A third party tells one character that the other loves them.

tropes.name: Love Epiphany
tropes.def: One character realizes they're in love with the other. Green-Eyed Epiphany

tropes.name: Love Revelation Epiphany
tropes.def: ...after said other character confesses their own love.

tropes.name: Love Triangle
tropes.def: Two people love the same person, and only one person can have them.

tropes.name: MacGuffin Escort Mission
tropes.def: The good guys get the MacGuffin early, so the rest of the story is about them transporting it somewhere else without losing it.

tropes.name: Macho Disaster Expedition
tropes.def: Men and women go on a stereotypically male-oriented activity. The guys fail miserably due to arrogance and have to be saved by the women.

tropes.name: Madden Into Misanthropy
tropes.def: The annoyance of having to put up with certain people causes a person to develop a hatred of humanity.

tropes.name: Made a Slave
tropes.def: A character is sold or forced into slavery, and must escape, be rescued or learn to live with it.

tropes.name: Mail-Order Bride
tropes.def: "Ordering" a spouse over the Internet.

tropes.name: Main Character Final Boss
tropes.def: The game ends with the main character becoming the final boss, requiring their party to either fight to free them or kill them.

tropes.name: Make Up or Break Up
tropes.def: A couple has to choose whether to stay together or break up.

tropes.name: Man in the Iron Mask
tropes.def: A character is held prisoner by another, even though the captive threatens the captor by his very existence.

tropes.name: Man Versus Machine
tropes.def: Conflict between humans and robots.

tropes.name: Mandatory Unretirement
tropes.def: A character is forced to do a job they have already given up.

tropes.name: Meet Cute
tropes.def: Crash-Into Hello

tropes.name: Mental Story
tropes.def: A story that focuses on what's going on in someone's head.

tropes.name: Minor Crime Reveals Major Plot
tropes.def: Someone investigates a minor crime, but finds something much bigger going on behind it.

tropes.name: Missed the Call
tropes.def: The Chosen One missed their opportunity for the adventure.

tropes.name: Mission from God
tropes.def: When someone believes their goals were given to them by orders from God.

tropes.name: Moby Schtick
tropes.def: A Whole-Plot Reference to Moby-Dick and its story of a monomaniacal captain hunting a whale.

tropes.name: Mockstery Tale
tropes.def: One or more characters try to solve a mystery but then the mystery turns out to be nonexistent, unimportant, or unsolvable and it turns into psychological horror or similar.

tropes.name: Model Scam
tropes.def: A woman is lured into a trap (usually involving rape) under the pretense of a model shoot.

tropes.name: Moment Killer
tropes.def: Someone else ruins a romantic moment between the pair.

tropes.name: More than Mind Control
tropes.def: A character did something evil because of Brainwashing but they also did it willingly, if only slightly.

tropes.name: My Biological Clock Is Ticking
tropes.def: When a woman gets to be of a certain age, getting married and/or having babies right away becomes of utmost concern to her.

tropes.name: My Death Is Just the Beginning
tropes.def: Villain lets themselves die so their plan may continue.

tropes.name: Naïve Newcomer
tropes.def: A newcomer who is inexperienced and has trouble fitting in.

tropes.name: Never Learned to Read
tropes.def: A character is revealed to be illiterate and in many cases will try to overcome it.

tropes.name: New Ability Addiction
tropes.def: A character gets a new skill or piece of kit and has the urge to use it.

tropes.name: New Super Power
tropes.def: A character gains a new superpower.

tropes.name: Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!
tropes.def: The hero tries to save the day, but their efforts end up making things worse.

tropes.name: Nightmare of Normality
tropes.def: A supernatural character is deluded into thinking that they're ordinary and must find a way to awaken from the illusion.

tropes.name: Nitro Express
tropes.def: Hauling unstable explosives over dangerous terrain. What could possibly go wrong?

tropes.name: No Doubt the Years Have Changed Me
tropes.def: A character is unrecognizable after being away for many years.

tropes.name: No Guy Wants an Amazon
tropes.def: Men don't want to be with women who can beat them up.

tropes.name: Noah's Story Arc
tropes.def: Evacuating a large population of people and animals in order to survive an impending disaster.

tropes.name: Not a Date
tropes.def: They spend time together, but one or both of them specify that it's not a date.

tropes.name: Not Himself
tropes.def: A character isn't acting like they normally would, usually as a result of an Evil Twin , "Freaky Friday" Flip , or Demonic Possession .

tropes.name: Not Just a Tournament
tropes.def: A tournament with a sinister ulterior purpose.

tropes.name: Not Quite Back to Normal
tropes.def: A transformed character retains some residual effects even after reverting back to normal.

tropes.name: Not the First Victim
tropes.def: A predator had victims before the apparent "first" victim.

tropes.name: Off the Wagon
tropes.def: An alcoholic or drug addict tries to quit but then starts it up again.

tropes.name: Off to See the Wizard
tropes.def: Plots inspired by or parodying The Wonderful Wizard of Oz , especially the 1939 film adaptation .

tropes.name: Official Kiss
tropes.def: Two characters kiss, signaling a Relationship Upgrade .

tropes.name: Older Hero vs. Younger Villain
tropes.def: The hero is old or borderline old, while the villain is relatively young.

tropes.name: On the Money
tropes.def: Characters in need of money find a contest, inheritance, or job offering the exact amount they need.

tropes.name: One Crazy Night
tropes.def: Plans for a quiet peaceful night turns into a problem that keeps getting worse.

tropes.name: Out of Job, Into the Plot
tropes.def: The protagonist loses their job shortly before or after the action begins.

tropes.name: Passing the Torch
tropes.def: The story ends with the hero choosing someone to continue their legacy.

tropes.name: Peer Pressure Makes You Evil
tropes.def: When a character's morally shady friends influence him to lower his own moral standards.

tropes.name: Penny Among Diamonds
tropes.def: A commoner (or poor person) is thrust into rich culture without becoming rich themselves.

tropes.name: Perfection Is Addictive
tropes.def: Once you experience complete, utter perfection, it's almost impossible to settle for anything less.

tropes.name: Physical Therapy Plot
tropes.def: A character gets severely injured to the point of disability and begins physical therapy. The character tries to become mobile again by pushing themselves physically and mentally.

tropes.name: Pilgrimage
tropes.def: A travel to Holy Ground or for a holy purpose.

tropes.name: Pirate Booty
tropes.def: Troves of gold and jewels plundered by pirates and buried in faraway places to await discovery.

tropes.name: Plague of Good Fortune
tropes.def: A character has an amazing series of good things happen to them despite not wanting it to.

tropes.name: Plot-Driving Secret
tropes.def: The entire plot of a work depends on no one knowing the truth.

tropes.name: Plot-Inciting Infidelity
tropes.def: When the plot of a story is kickstarted by having the protagonist catch their partner cheating on them.

tropes.name: Plot Tailored to the Party
tropes.def: Each protagonist has to overcome an obstacle specifically matched to their specialty.

tropes.name: Plot-Triggering Book
tropes.def: A character either discovers a book or is given one which kicks off the plot.

tropes.name: Plot-Triggering Death
tropes.def: A character's death at the outset of a story puts its main plot into motion.

tropes.name: Poison and Cure Gambit
tropes.def: Manipulating someone into doing what you want by poisoning them and refusing to give them the antidote until they do as you say.

tropes.name: Police Brutality Gambit
tropes.def: Someone accuses the police of Police Brutality as part of a Wounded Gazelle Gambit .

tropes.name: Portal Book
tropes.def: A book that can transport someone to the world of its story, or the location that is represented in it.

tropes.name: Possessive Paradise
tropes.def: A place that prevents you from leaving.

tropes.name: Pre-Meeting
tropes.def: The main character meets a random person who turns out to be someone important.

tropes.name: Premature Empowerment
tropes.def: A superpowered group want to induct a new member through Super-Empowering .

tropes.name: Prevent the War
tropes.def: Heroes try to prevent a war from occurring.

tropes.name: Pride Before a Fall
tropes.def: A character starts out as a insufferable jerk until something happens that causes them to become humble.

tropes.name: Prince and Pauper
tropes.def: Two identical people from different backgrounds switch lives.

tropes.name: Princess for a Day
tropes.def: When a woman dresses up as an upper-class person.

tropes.name: Prodigal Family
tropes.def: Estranged family members show up to complicate a character's life.

tropes.name: Prodigal Hero
tropes.def: A character runs away from home, lives in exile, and returns home to save the day.

tropes.name: Protagonist Journey to Villain
tropes.def: The story is about how the protagonist ends up becoming evil.

tropes.name: Protect This House
tropes.def: The hero's home comes under attack.

tropes.name: Pursued Protagonist
tropes.def: When a work opens with someone being chased.

tropes.name: Puzzle Thriller
tropes.def: A plot centered around uncovering roles to a game.

tropes.name: Pygmalion Plot
tropes.def: A character falls in love with their own creation.

tropes.name: Pygmalion Snap Back
tropes.def: A character who was changed by another character to fit their ideals reverts to their original self.

tropes.name: Quest for a Wish
tropes.def: The characters go on an adventure to have a single wish granted.

tropes.name: Quest for Identity
tropes.def: A character tries to rediscover who they are.

tropes.name: Quest for Sex
tropes.def: A whole story focused on a man trying to get laid.

tropes.name: Quest for the Rest
tropes.def: A character who is thought to be the Last of His Kind ventures off to search for others like him.

tropes.name: Quest to the West
tropes.def: A character's journey is associated with them heading west.

tropes.name: Race Against the Clock
tropes.def: The heroes have to do something to stop the countdown, or else the consequences will be catastrophic.

tropes.name: Radish Cure
tropes.def: Someone wants something forbidden, and then they're granted it in a way that puts them off of it forever.

tropes.name: Rage Against the Heavens
tropes.def: A character wants the gods to pay for what they've done.

tropes.name: Rage Within the Machine
tropes.def: A character is loyally part of a party or division linked to the government, but begins to doubt if said party/division is right about their beliefs or policies.

tropes.name: Rags to Riches
tropes.def: A character goes from being poor or living modestly to being wealthy and successful.

tropes.name: Rags to Royalty
tropes.def: A character is elevated (or restored) to nobility.

tropes.name: Rash Promise
tropes.def: A character swears to do something without much thought and must choose between keeping their word or suffering the consequences of their lack of foresight.

tropes.name: "Ray of Hope" Ending
tropes.def: An ending that would normally be a Downer Ending , but shows that there's still hope left for the heroes.

tropes.name: Really 17 Years Old
tropes.def: A minor pretends to be an adult.

tropes.name: "Rear Window" Investigation
tropes.def: A character suspects another character of a crime and waits for that person to leave their home so they can sneak in and look for clues or evidence.

tropes.name: "Rear Window" Witness
tropes.def: A character is caught in a situation where they witness a crime (or what he thinks is a crime) and is powerless to do anything to stop it.

tropes.name: Rebuilt Pedestal
tropes.def: Someone loses their respect for a hero, but starts liking them again after their idol proves that being more flawed than their fan assumed does not mean they're a bad person.

tropes.name: Recruit Teenagers with Attitude
tropes.def: Instead of trained adults, teenagers save the day.

tropes.name: Red Pill, Blue Pill
tropes.def: You have two choices: heed the call, or continue living like a regular person.

tropes.name: Redeeming Replacement
tropes.def: A villain gets a heroic successor who aims to do good in order to make up for their predecessor's crimes.

tropes.name: Redemption Quest
tropes.def: The villain goes on a quest to atone for their misdeeds.

tropes.name: Refusal of the Call
tropes.def: The Chosen One willfully refuses to heed the call. Got Volunteered : A person is forced to join against their will.

tropes.name: Refusal of the Second Call
tropes.def: The hero of the original is available to save the day again in the sequel, but refuses to help.

tropes.name: Refused by the Call
tropes.def: You want The Call, the Call doesn't want you.

tropes.name: Regular Caller
tropes.def: The Chosen One heeds many calls.

tropes.name: Reincarnation Romance
tropes.def: The two characters were a couple in their past lives.

tropes.name: Rescue Arc
tropes.def: A story arc centered around saving someone's life.

tropes.name: Rescue Romance
tropes.def: One character is rescuing the other.

tropes.name: Rescued from the Underworld
tropes.def: Rescuing someone who is trapped in the afterlife.

tropes.name: Resigned to the Call
tropes.def: The Chosen One heeds the call reluctantly.

tropes.name: Revenge
tropes.def: To get back at the one who wronged you.

tropes.name: Riding into the Sunset
tropes.def: Character goes off into the distance while the sun is setting.

tropes.name: Right Man in the Wrong Place
tropes.def: Some guy is asked to heed the call. Not because it's their call to heed, but because they really need a Chosen One right now.

tropes.name: Rightful King Returns
tropes.def: The proper ruler comes back to fix everything after things have gone to hell in their absence.

tropes.name: Rip Van Winkle
tropes.def: A character sleeps for several decades.

tropes.name: River of Insanity
tropes.def: Any river voyage or wilderness journey is a doomed expedition in which the characters alternately die, go mad, get lost, go native, or otherwise barely live to tell the tale.

tropes.name: Road Trip Plot
tropes.def: Everyone goes on a road trip. Hilarity Ensues .

tropes.name: Road Trip Romance
tropes.def: Two characters traveling together eventually fall in love.

tropes.name: Roaring Rampage of Rescue
tropes.def: The character stops at nothing to save their loved one, including mowing anyone in their path.

tropes.name: Roaring Rampage of Revenge
tropes.def: A character is pushed so far over the edge and goes completely ballistic on those that hurt them.

tropes.name: Robbing the Mob Bank
tropes.def: A thief steals from another criminal, who tries to get the thief caught.

tropes.name: Rogue Juror
tropes.def: One juror's opinion goes against the others', and it's up to them to change their minds.

tropes.name: Romantic Fake–Real Turn
tropes.def: A fake romance becomes real.

tropes.name: Romantic Rain
tropes.def: Umbrella of Togetherness

tropes.name: Roommate Drama
tropes.def: Characters share a room or house, and things go wrong.

tropes.name: Run for the Border
tropes.def: A criminal tries to escape the law by fleeing to another country.

tropes.name: Save the Day, Turn Away
tropes.def: Someone saves the day but has to dump their love interest.

tropes.name: Save the Princess
tropes.def: An Excuse Plot for rescuing a princess that has been kidnapped.

tropes.name: "Save the World" Climax
tropes.def: A plot that initially wasn't about saving the world is so by the end.

tropes.name: Saving Christmas
tropes.def: Someone has to prevent Christmas from being ruined for everyone who celebrates the holiday.

tropes.name: Saving the Orphanage
tropes.def: The hero has to stop a heartless business exec who wants to destroy a local Orphanage of Love .

tropes.name: Saving the World
tropes.def: The heroes try to save the world's population from the villains evil plan.

tropes.name: Saving the World with Art
tropes.def: A character uses a form of art in order to solve a problem or save the world.

tropes.name: Scarpia Ultimatum
tropes.def: Someone is blackmailed into having sex with a person who threatens to hurt someone they care about if they refuse.

tropes.name: Scavenger Hunt
tropes.def: Characters play a game where they find a list of items before a set deadline.

tropes.name: School for Scheming
tropes.def: A school that is used as a cover for an elaborate plot-centric scheme.

tropes.name: Schrödinger's Butterfly
tropes.def: Stories where it's never completely clear whether everything is real or not.

tropes.name: "Scooby-Doo" Hoax
tropes.def: A monster is revealed to actually be a disguised criminal pretending to be one.

tropes.name: Screening the Call
tropes.def: The Chosen One misses the call due to a character's meddling.

tropes.name: Screw the Rules, I'm Doing What's Right!
tropes.def: Deliberately defying rules because they go against doing what is clearly the right thing.

tropes.name: Seal the Breach
tropes.def: Characters are at or travel to a place that has a breach, whether it is a hole in a dam or a gateway to Hell.

tropes.name: Sealed with a Kiss
tropes.def: The Official Couple gets The Big Damn Kiss near or at the end of the story.

tropes.name: Secret Pet Plot
tropes.def: A character adopts a pet and tries to hide it.

tropes.name: Secret Relationship
tropes.def: Characters are in a relationship that they don't want their friends and family to know about.

tropes.name: Secret Test of Character
tropes.def: The hero is then told that by forfeiting the challenge in a certain way is exactly what was needed to triumph, and that it was actually a test of character, and they have passed with flying colors.

tropes.name: Send in the Search Team
tropes.def: Something has gone wrong at an unknown location, and a seach party is gathered to find out what happened.

tropes.name: Separated at Birth
tropes.def: Two normally unrelated characters are revealed to be twin siblings raised apart from each other.

tropes.name: Serendipity Shock
tropes.def: A character suddenly gets the one thing they've always wanted, and is able to keep it permanently.

tropes.name: Serial Killer
tropes.def: There's a murderer on the loose, and people are dying one by one. Can the heroes stop the killer before they strike again?

tropes.name: Set Right What Once Went Wrong
tropes.def: Altering the past to prevent bad things from ever occurring.

tropes.name: Settling the Frontier
tropes.def: Standard Western plot involving people establishing a colony or settlement in a previously unknown land.

tropes.name: Sex as Rite-of-Passage
tropes.def: Characters set out to get themselves laid.

tropes.name: Sex Equals Love
tropes.def: Characters who are in a sexual relationship but not in love will fall in love eventually.

tropes.name: Sex for Services
tropes.def: Trading sexual favors for non-sexual favors.

tropes.name: Sexy Man, Instant Harem
tropes.def: A man who is The Casanova will often attract women.

tropes.name: Ship Tease
tropes.def: The pair have a sweet moment together, hinting at future romance. Caught in the Rain

tropes.name: Shipwreck Start
tropes.def: Protagonist is shipwrecked to start the story.

tropes.name: Shoot the Shaggy Dog
tropes.def: The story ends with the protagonist dying and rubs salt in the wound by revealing their efforts to be pointless.

tropes.name: Shut Up, Hannibal!
tropes.def: The hero gives a defiant response to the villain mocking the hero's idealism or the villain justifying their immoral actions.

tropes.name: Sink or Swim Fatherhood
tropes.def: A character unexpectedly becomes a parent and must learn on the job.

tropes.name: Sinking Ship Scenario
tropes.def: Catastrophic damage to a large vehicle forces the characters to struggle to survive.

tropes.name: Skipping School
tropes.def: A student decides not to go to school and goes off to do something else instead.

tropes.name: Sleep Learning
tropes.def: Someone tries to learn information in their sleep.

tropes.name: Slow and Steady Wins the Race
tropes.def: A character loses a race for most of the story, but wins at the end

tropes.name: Slumber Party Ploy
tropes.def: In order to do something or go somewhere they were prohibited from, kids lie to their parents that they are staying over at each others' houses.

tropes.name: Small-Minded Villain
tropes.def: A villain who never rises above petty crimes despite their talent and powers.

tropes.name: Snipe Hunt
tropes.def: A character is tricked into searching for a nonexistent thing.

tropes.name: Snowballing Threat
tropes.def: Must stop something urgently before it becomes too powerful.

tropes.name: Snowed-In
tropes.def: Snow is packed around your building, vehicle, etc., and you are stuck for a while.

tropes.name: So Near, Yet So Far
tropes.def: You're already at your destination, but can't do what you need to.

tropes.name: Someone to Remember Him By
tropes.def: A woman turns out to be pregnant with the child of her recently deceased lover.

tropes.name: Sorcerer's Apprentice Plot
tropes.def: A young ward's attempts to be like his boss becomes too much for him to handle.

tropes.name: Speak Now or Forever Hold Your Peace
tropes.def: Dramatically interrupting a wedding.

tropes.name: Speed Dating
tropes.def: A character tries speed dating in order to meet someone.

tropes.name: Spelling Bee
tropes.def: A competition where the characters try to spell words.

tropes.name: Split and Reunion
tropes.def: A Split Personality gets separated. When it reunites, issues are resolved an teamwork has improved.

tropes.name: Spot the Impostor
tropes.def: One character is seen with their impersonator, resulting in their friends having to figure out which is which.

tropes.name: Standard Hero Reward
tropes.def: After saving the day, The Hero is rewarded with marriage to a princess.

tropes.name: Start My Own
tropes.def: A character is disgruntled with the way a certain group is run, so they decide to start their own.

tropes.name: Start of Darkness
tropes.def: The moment in a villain's life where they started to become evil.

tropes.name: Start to Corpse
tropes.def: The story begins with a dead body being discovered or someone being killed.

tropes.name: Starter Villain
tropes.def: The first villain the hero fights, usually only relevant in serving as the first threat the hero successfully thwarts.

tropes.name: Starter Villain Stays
tropes.def: The hero's first villain subsequently sticks around and continues to be a prominent enemy.

tropes.name: Starts with a Suicide
tropes.def: The story begins with someone committing or attempting to commit suicide.

tropes.name: Starts with Their Funeral
tropes.def: The story begins with a funeral before explaining how the person died.

tropes.name: Step One: Escape
tropes.def: The initial goal is getting out of a room.

tropes.name: Stern Chase
tropes.def: The protagonist is being pursued and must stay in motion.

tropes.name: Stock Evil Overlord Tactics
tropes.def: Common evil plans that villains come up with.

tropes.name: Stone Soup
tropes.def: Manipulating others via feigned eccentric behavior.

tropes.name: Storming the Castle
tropes.def: Assaulting the Big Bad's home base.

tropes.name: Stranger in a Familiar Land
tropes.def: The hero returns home, but their home has changed so much that it's no longer the same place it was when they originally left.

tropes.name: Stranger in a Strange School
tropes.def: An Ordinary High-School Student who winds up attending an Extranormal Institute .

tropes.name: "Strangers on a Train"-Plot Murder
tropes.def: Two people make a deal to commit each other's heinous crime/difficult task.

tropes.name: Stumbled Into the Plot
tropes.def: The protagonist is the one who finds the Inciting Incident instead of being chosen or summoned .

tropes.name: Stumbling Upon the Lost Wizard
tropes.def: The Protagonist(s) accidentally find a character of great importance when they become lost themselves.

tropes.name: Succession Crisis
tropes.def: The king dies and no one knows who will succeed him.

tropes.name: Sudden Downer Ending
tropes.def: The story abruptly ends on a bleak note.

tropes.name: Sudden Intelligence
tropes.def: A character is abruptly given an IQ boost.

tropes.name: Sugar Apocalypse
tropes.def: When a genuine Sugar Bowl suffers a horrifying disaster that destroys its peaceful innocence.

tropes.name: Suicide Mission
tropes.def: A mission will almost certainly end in death for whoever accepts it.

tropes.name: Summon Everyman Hero
tropes.def: An average person is brought into another for a wacky adventure.

tropes.name: Superpowers for a Day
tropes.def: A normal person temporarily gains special powers.

tropes.name: Superhero Origin
tropes.def: The story of how a superhero gained their powers and decided to fight crime.

tropes.name: Supporting Characters Say Goodbye
tropes.def: The finale includes the protagonist saying good-bye to other characters.

tropes.name: Surprise Party
tropes.def: A surprise party is held to celebrate an occasion.

tropes.name: Surprisingly Happy Ending
tropes.def: You have braced for a Bittersweet Ending , but things turned out a lot better than you expected.

tropes.name: Survival Through Self-Sacrifice
tropes.def: A character chooses to sacrifice his or her life, and is spared for doing so.

tropes.name: Symbolic Hero Rebirth
tropes.def: Death and rebirth symbolism accompany plotlines of hero who can no longer ignore their destiny.

tropes.name: Sympathetic with Added Context
tropes.def: A character seems unsympathetic, but added context reveals that they are.

tropes.name: Systematic Villain Takedown
tropes.def: A group of villains is taken down one by one during the course of an arc or a story.

tropes.name: Tag-Along Actor
tropes.def: An actor researches the role of a special profession by shadowing their real life counterpart.

tropes.name: Tag Team Suicide
tropes.def: Two people kill themselves because a failure to communicate causes them both to think the other has died.

tropes.name: Take Care of the Kids
tropes.def: Someone is dying and asks another person to take care of a person (usually a kid as kids are more likely to need care).

tropes.name: Take My Hand!
tropes.def: One character is about to fall off a cliff and another tries to catch their hand.

tropes.name: Take Up My Sword
tropes.def: The Chosen One dies, so someone else needs to heed his call.

tropes.name: Taking Over Heaven
tropes.def: Attacking Heaven and taking charge of it.

tropes.name: Taking Over the Town
tropes.def: The villains take over a town and steal from it.

tropes.name: Talent Contest
tropes.def: Characters participate in an amateur talent contest.

tropes.name: Talking Your Way Out
tropes.def: The hero is caught by the villains, but manages to use smooth talking to get away.

tropes.name: Teach Him Anger
tropes.def: A character who is normally the Nice Guy is taught by their friends to be more assertive.

tropes.name: Teacher/Student Romance
tropes.def: A student and a teacher get into a romantic or sexual relationship. Highly inadvisable in Real Life .

tropes.name: Technician Versus Performer
tropes.def: Two characters contrast each other because one is all about being accurate and the other just wants to have fun.

tropes.name: Ten Little Murder Victims
tropes.def: A group of people are stuck somewhere. One of them is a killer, the rest are potential victims.

tropes.name: The Bad Guy Wins
tropes.def: The villain succeeds in their plan and gets what they want.

tropes.name: The Big Race
tropes.def: Characters participate in a race.

tropes.name: The Breakfast Plot
tropes.def: A group of characters gets stuck together (in what may or may not be detention) and end up bonding.

tropes.name: The Cake Is a Lie
tropes.def: A promised reward turns out to be nothing but a lie.

tropes.name: The Call Has Bad Reception
tropes.def: The Chosen One can't do their mission properly because they don't have the whole picture.

tropes.name: The Call Knows Where You Live
tropes.def: If you refuse to go on this adventure, the adventure will burn your house down and make you go on it.

tropes.name: The Call Left a Message
tropes.def: Only the Chosen One is allowed to hear this message.

tropes.name: The Call Put Me on Hold
tropes.def: The Chosen One is the only Muggle among superhumans .

tropes.name: The Caper
tropes.def: A group of protagonists organize an elaborate robbery.

tropes.name: The Captivity Narrative
tropes.def: A Puritan girl is captured by Natives and has to resist their culture. Discredited and forgotten these days.

tropes.name: The Cavalry Arrives Late
tropes.def: The hero has reinforcements, but they don't show up until after the day is saved.

tropes.name: The Chain of Harm
tropes.def: A character who was abused unleashes the same kind of abuse on someone else.

tropes.name: The Chase
tropes.def: A plot centered on characters pursuing one another.

tropes.name: The Chooser of the One
tropes.def: The one that decides who The Chosen One is.

tropes.name: The Collector
tropes.def: People version of Collector of the Strange .

tropes.name: The Con
tropes.def: Scams used by criminals to illegally acquire money.

tropes.name: The Conspiracy
tropes.def: A secret plot from a powerful figure or group is happening and the protagonists investigate it.

tropes.name: The Day of Reckoning
tropes.def: The day when an Evil Overlord is destined to win.

tropes.name: The Dog Bites Back
tropes.def: An abused character finally has enough and enacts retribution on their tormentor(s).

tropes.name: The Dragons Come Back
tropes.def: A (sub)plot revolving around dragons or similar apex predators returning from exile/extinction.

tropes.name: The End of the Beginning
tropes.def: The end of the story is the beginning of a new era.

tropes.name: The Evils of Free Will
tropes.def: Someone feels that eliminating free will is the only way to achieve utopia.

tropes.name: The Fellowship Has Ended
tropes.def: The work ends with the main group of protagonists going their separate ways.

tropes.name: The Final Temptation
tropes.def: A character is given a chance to abandon his difficult life for a better one, complete with imagery for the latter.

tropes.name: The Game Never Stopped
tropes.def: The protagonists think the fake test has ended. It hasn't.

tropes.name: The Game Plays You
tropes.def: A seemingly harmless game haunts or harms the people that play it.

tropes.name: The Good Guys Always Win
tropes.def: The heroes always succeed in defeating the bad guys.

tropes.name: The Good Kingdom
tropes.def: , for a story in which the Hero must save the world from impending doom, and

tropes.name: The Great Repair
tropes.def: Characters have to repair a vehicle of some kind in order to escape the place where they're trapped.

tropes.name: The Greatest Story Never Told
tropes.def: A character does something heroic or awesome, but nobody hears about it.

tropes.name: The Grovel
tropes.def: (may involve an Anguished Declaration of Love )

tropes.name: The Hero
tropes.def: may be dissatisfied with the ordinary and express a desire for adventure. In musicals this can be expressed through an "I Want" Song or a Wanderlust Song .

tropes.name: The Hero Dies
tropes.def: The protagonist dies at the end of the story.

tropes.name: The Homeward Journey
tropes.def: The plot revolves around a character's journey to get back home .

tropes.name: The Idol's Blessing
tropes.def: Incompetent main character receives a boon from their idol, thus beginning their journey.

tropes.name: The Infiltration
tropes.def: A character must get "inside" a bad-guy organization and pass as a bad guy to accomplish a goal.

tropes.name: The Inspector Is Coming
tropes.def: A place of business prepares for a visit from an inspector or critic.

tropes.name: The Jungle Opera
tropes.def: A story that takes place in undiscovered or semidiscovered country in the present or "recent" past.

tropes.name: The Magic Comes Back
tropes.def: In a setting where magic has vanished, the magic ends up returning.

tropes.name: The Magic Goes Away
tropes.def: A story with magic in the setting ends with all the magic disappearing.

tropes.name: The Magnificent Seven Samurai
tropes.def: A helpless community under attack hires heroes (usually seven) to protect them, a Whole-Plot Reference to Seven Samurai .

tropes.name: The Makeover
tropes.def: Being transformed from ugly (or mundane) to beautiful.

tropes.name: The Man Behind the Curtain
tropes.def: An influential and previously unseen Big Bad is revealed to be pathetically weak.

tropes.name: The Migration
tropes.def: A homeless group migrate to a new home.

tropes.name: The Moving Experience
tropes.def: A character thinks their best friend is moving to another town and struggles to say goodbye.

tropes.name: The One Who Made It Out
tropes.def: A character who managed to rise above their less-than-stellar origins and become a success.

tropes.name: The Only One
tropes.def: The hero has to solve the problem because no one else can do it.

tropes.name: The Promised Land
tropes.def: The place that promises to be better than where we are. Where the Grass Is Greener .

tropes.name: The Queen Will Be Watching
tropes.def: Somebody very important will be in the audience at the Show Within a Show .

tropes.name: The Quest
tropes.def: The character leaves home, voluntarily or not, on a big adventure to recover something or search for someone.

tropes.name: The Secret Life of Nonhumans
tropes.def: Animals or even inanimate objects are secretly sentient and having their own society and lives unbeknown to humans.

tropes.name: The Show Must Go On
tropes.def: No matter what problems occur during a live performance, the characters do what they can to keep the show going.

tropes.name: The Siege
tropes.def: The good guys must hold off an overwhelming enemy threat against impossible odds.

tropes.name: The So-Called Coward
tropes.def: A character is passive and non-violent, making them branded a coward by everyone, only for something to happen that proves otherwise.

tropes.name: The Story That Never Was
tropes.def: The solution to the story's conflict is to completely undo the events via Cosmic Retcon .

tropes.name: The Trap Parents
tropes.def: An orphan gains some parents that don't want them to hang around their friends.

tropes.name: The Un-Reveal
tropes.def: Even when it looks like the big secret will be revealed, it never is.

tropes.name: The Temptress
tropes.def: a figure that tries to derail the journey and/or corrupt the hero.

tropes.name: The Villain Must Be Punished
tropes.def: The villain must pay for their crimes; merely foiling their plans isn't enough.

tropes.name: Their First Time
tropes.def: The first time two people had sex in their entire lives.

tropes.name: There Can Be Only One
tropes.def: A group of characters have to kill each other until only one remains.

tropes.name: There's No Place Like Home
tropes.def: A character's main goal is to go back home.

tropes.name: Third-Act Misunderstanding
tropes.def: Mistaken for Cheating

tropes.name: Third Act Stupidity
tropes.def: The heroes or villains (or both) start acting stupid to sustain conflict in the climax.

tropes.name: This Looks Like a Job for Aquaman!
tropes.def: A character with not-so-useful powers is put in a situation where they'd actually be helpful.

tropes.name: Thriller on the Express
tropes.def: A crime/espionage/murder mystery story centered around a moving train setting.

tropes.name: Throne Room Throwdown
tropes.def: a climatic fight scene occurs in a throne room.

tropes.name: Through the Eyes of Madness
tropes.def: Crazy people see the world differently from normal people.

tropes.name: Time Travel Escape
tropes.def: Saving a dead person via time travel.

tropes.name: Time-Travel Romance
tropes.def: Romance between people from different time periods.

tropes.name: Titanomachy, Round Two
tropes.def: Someone's trying to free the Titans of Greek Mythology to take out the Gods.

tropes.name: To Be a Master
tropes.def: The protagonist's main goal is to be the very best, like no one ever was .

tropes.name: To Hell and Back
tropes.def: Part of the hero's mission involves entering Hell or a similar place.

tropes.name: Together in Death
tropes.def: (exit point) Reincarnation Romance (Go back to start )

tropes.name: Tomato in the Mirror
tropes.def: A character discovers that they are not what they think they are.

tropes.name: Tomato Surprise
tropes.def: Something is known to the characters in-universe, but is revealed to the audience as a twist.

tropes.name: Tontine
tropes.def: A group of people make an agreement that the valuables they've found will go to the last surviving member of the group.

tropes.name: Torch the Franchise and Run
tropes.def: The creator(s) deliberately make it so that the work ends in a way that it's impossible to continue the story any further, often by destroying the characters and setting to such a degree that continuations aren't viable due to there being nothing left for future writers and creators to use.

tropes.name: Tournament Arc
tropes.def: A plot arc consisting of characters fighting each other in a competition.

tropes.name: Train Job
tropes.def: Boarding a train in order to steal from it.

tropes.name: Training "Accident"
tropes.def: A character undergoes special training only for something to go horrible wrong .

tropes.name: Training the Peaceful Villagers
tropes.def: The Hero trains a local village to fight back against an advancing army.

tropes.name: Transformed Ever After
tropes.def: The story ends with a character being permanently transformed - or remaining that way.

tropes.name: Trapped in TV Land
tropes.def: Someone gets trapped inside a work of fiction.

tropes.name: Trapped in the Past
tropes.def: Someone accidentally ends up in the past without knowing how to come back.

tropes.name: Trapped-with-Monster Plot
tropes.def: Characters are in a Closed Circle with something hunting them.

tropes.name: Trauma Button Ending
tropes.def: A character has a reaction to a trigger that has to do with events that they just went through.

tropes.name: Treasure Map
tropes.def: A map leading to hidden treasure.

tropes.name: Trend Aesop
tropes.def: A character learns a lesson about trying to fit in with the crowd.

tropes.name: Tricked into Signing
tropes.def: A character is tricked into signing an important document.

tropes.name: Trippy Finale Syndrome
tropes.def: The finale takes place in some trippy and abstract realm.

tropes.name: Triumphant Reprise
tropes.def: A tragic song in a musical production gets a more optimistic and triumphant reprise later on. In many cases, the song's brighter counterpart is sung at the ending to further emphasize the protagonist's victory in overcoming the conflict.

tropes.name: Trouble Follows You Home
tropes.def: A character makes it home after escaping trouble, only to find trouble waiting for them there.

tropes.name: Trouble from the Past
tropes.def: A plot where future generations have to deal with the mess made by their civilization in the past.

tropes.name: Troublemaking New Pet
tropes.def: New pet is up to no good, blames their actions on the older.

tropes.name: "Truman Show" Plot
tropes.def: Someone discovers that their life was part of a film or television show without their knowledge.

tropes.name: Turn in Your Badge
tropes.def: A cop who has stepped over the line is ordered to turn in their badge and gun.

tropes.name: Turned Against Their Masters
tropes.def: Artificially derived beings turn against their creators.

tropes.name: Twelfth Night Adventure
tropes.def: A character becomes a Wholesome Crossdresser to integrate himself/herself into the setting.

tropes.name: Twin Switch
tropes.def: Twins swap roles with each other, such as with a Two-Timer Date . Hilarity Ensues if they are Polar Opposite Twins .

tropes.name: Twisting the Prophecy
tropes.def: Knowingly fulfilling a prophecy in a way that creates a favourable outcome.

tropes.name: Two Dun It
tropes.def: A reveal where two people are responsible for a crime.

tropes.name: Two Roads Before You
tropes.def: Being presented with a choice between two or more mutually exclusive options.

tropes.name: Two-Timer Date
tropes.def: A character schedules dates with two different people at the same time.

tropes.name: Unbelievable Source Plot
tropes.def: A plot where the protagonist relies on a supernatural source of information to solve crimes.

tropes.name: Undercover as Lovers
tropes.def: Two spies pose as lovers as they go undercover.

tropes.name: Undercover Cop Reveal
tropes.def: A person turns out to be an undercover cop.

tropes.name: Unexpected Character
tropes.def: The work features a character in the franchise that audiences did not anticipate to be involved.

tropes.name: Unique Moment Ruined
tropes.def: A highly anticipated moment or event is ruined by something.

tropes.name: Unlocking the Talent
tropes.def: A character has a skill that they never use and have to learn to use it to their advantage.

tropes.name: Unreliable Narrator
tropes.def: It is hinted that the narrator may be exaggerating or glossing over parts of the story, if they weren't just outright lying.

tropes.name: Unresolved Sexual Tension
tropes.def: Almost Holding Hands

tropes.name: Unsettling Gender-Reveal
tropes.def: Someone is disturbed by the revelation that a woman is actually a man in drag.

tropes.name: Unsympathetic with Added Context
tropes.def: A character seems sympathetic, but added context reveals that they aren't.

tropes.name: Untrusting Community
tropes.def: A whole town full of people who don't like you.

tropes.name: Unwanted Glasses Plot
tropes.def: A character discovers they need glasses, but refuses to wear them because they look uncool.

tropes.name: Unwanted Healing
tropes.def: A character has a terrible illness, but refuses to accept treatment for it.

tropes.name: Unwanted Rescue
tropes.def: The Hero saves someone in trouble only to learn that they didn't want to be rescued.

tropes.name: Unwanted Revival
tropes.def: A resurrected person isn't happy that they've been brought back to life.

tropes.name: Unwitting Test Subject
tropes.def: A thinking subject (human, sapient animal, ect.) is part of a scientific experiment without their knowledge or consent.

tropes.name: Usurping the Alpha Bitch
tropes.def: The story ends with the new girl overthrowing the Alpha Bitch and taking her place on the social throne.

tropes.name: Utopia Justifies the Means
tropes.def: A situation where the goal of the Big Bad is the creation of a better world for everyone as a whole, no matter what the cost.

tropes.name: Vampire Detective Series
tropes.def: Vampires who fight crime.

tropes.name: Vampire Refugee
tropes.def: Someone turned by a vampire decides to find and kill the vampire that bit them to reverse the transformation.

tropes.name: Vanishing Village
tropes.def: A location that only appears or is accessible for certain periods of time.

tropes.name: Velvet Revolution
tropes.def: The conflict is resolved in peaceful and non-violent revolution.

tropes.name: Very Special Episode
tropes.def: An episode dedicating to dealing with a serious subject not usually brought up in other shows.

tropes.name: Vicious Cycle
tropes.def: Bad events occur regularly.

tropes.name: Victorious Loser
tropes.def: The protagonist loses everything around him/her, but the protagonist's spirit isn't broken and achieves his/her goal.

tropes.name: Victory Is Boring
tropes.def: Achieving one's goal has the downside of no longer having the fun of trying to achieve it.

tropes.name: Victory Sex
tropes.def: Characters celebrate their victory with sex.

tropes.name: Villain-Beating Artifact
tropes.def: The villain is invincible to everything but a specific artifact.

tropes.name: Villainous Legacy
tropes.def: The villain has inspired evil long after they passed away.

tropes.name: Visit by Divorced Dad
tropes.def: A divorced father visits his children.

tropes.name: Wake-Up Call
tropes.def: Something occurs that forces a character to develop out of complacency, get their act together, learn a lesson, or some combination thereof.

tropes.name: Wake Up, Go to School, Save the World
tropes.def: A Kid Hero has to juggle heroics and their personal life.

tropes.name: Walking the Earth
tropes.def: A character travels the earth, never returning home.

tropes.name: War Arc
tropes.def: A Story Arc that concerns two or more large-scale factions (city-sized at least) in conflict with one another.

tropes.name: War Comes Home
tropes.def: When a war spreads to the hero's homeland, making it personal.

tropes.name: War for Fun and Profit
tropes.def: Instigating a war for one's own material benefit.

tropes.name: War from Another World
tropes.def: When a world and its inhabitants unwillingly gets drawn into a war from elsewhere.

tropes.name: War Was Beginning
tropes.def: The story begins with a war starting.

tropes.name: Was It Really Worth It?
tropes.def: A character finally succeeds in their goal, but doesn't enjoy their victory because they're ashamed of what they had to do to make it possible.

tropes.name: Was Too Hard on Him
tropes.def: A character feels sad and guilty over scolding or harshly punishing someone.

tropes.name: Water Source Tampering
tropes.def: Villains tamper with the water supply.

tropes.name: Wayback Trip
tropes.def: The protagonist/s have to fix a change in history but the change has happened for seemingly no reason.

tropes.name: We Are Not Going Through That Again
tropes.def: The Chosen One heeded one calling and refuses to heed another.

tropes.name: We Need to Get Proof
tropes.def: The heroes discover the bad guy is up to no good, but need to find a way for others to believe them.

tropes.name: We Want Our Idiot Back!
tropes.def: A formerly idiotic character becomes smart, and their peers want to change them back for one reason or another.

tropes.name: We Want Our Jerk Back!
tropes.def: A mean character becomes nicer or leaves, resulting in everyone else deciding that things were better when the guy was still around or still a jerk.

tropes.name: We Would Have Told You, But...
tropes.def: A character has to be kept in the dark about something in order for the plan to work out.

tropes.name: Wealthy Ever After
tropes.def: The story ends with a character becoming wealthy.

tropes.name: Wedding Bells... for Someone Else
tropes.def: Two people look like they are about to be married, only for it to turn out they're guests at someone else's wedding.

tropes.name: Wedding Finale
tropes.def: Someone gets married at the end of the story.

tropes.name: Wedding Smashers
tropes.def: A rush to stop a wedding.

tropes.name: Weddings for Everyone
tropes.def: Multiple couples get married at the end of the story.

tropes.name: Welcome Episode
tropes.def: The first episode begins with one of the main characters meeting the rest of the cast for the first time and being given information that is also beneficial for the audience.

tropes.name: Atonement With the Father
tropes.def: George Lucas loved this step. Oedipus probably didn't. Variants include a final showdown with an Archnemesis Dad (sometimes still ending in atonement if Death Equals Redemption ) and Calling the Old Man Out .

tropes.name: Well-Intentioned Replacement
tropes.def: Replacing an important artifact after it has been destroyed or lost.

tropes.name: Wham Episode
tropes.def: An episode that suddenly changes the series' tone from then on. Wham Episode Fallout : An episode where the consequences of the Wham! Episode are shown.

tropes.name: Wham Line
tropes.def: The mood of the work changes abruptly all because of a single line of dialogue.

tropes.name: Wham Shot
tropes.def: A single scene changes everything.

tropes.name: What Could Possibly Go Wrong?
tropes.def: The dreaded words that, when spoken, will certainly lead to disaster.

tropes.name: "What's Inside?" Plot
tropes.def: Characters try to figure out what is hidden inside a locked box or closet.

tropes.name: When It All Began
tropes.def: The one moment or event that caused everything else in the story to be the way it is.

tropes.name: "Where Are They Now?" Epilogue
tropes.def: The ending shows what became of the characters after the events of the story.

tropes.name: Where I Was Born and Razed
tropes.def: A character destroys their own hometown.

tropes.name: Where It All Began
tropes.def: The hero's journey ends the same location where it began.

tropes.name: White Man's Burden
tropes.def: A well-to-do white character selflessly works to help an unfortunate person of color.

tropes.name: Who Will Take The Kids?
tropes.def: Parents wonder who would look after the kids if something bad happened.

tropes.name: Whodunnit to Me?
tropes.def: Someone who survives or is resurrected after an attempt to do them in tries to figure out who their murderer or would-be murderer was.

tropes.name: Why Would Anyone Take Him Back?
Win-Win Ending
tropes.def: Everyone gets a happy ending.

tropes.name: Witch Hunt
tropes.def: A search, often misguided, for a witch hidden among the community.

tropes.name: Withholding the Cure
tropes.def: Someone prevents the cure for a disease from getting to the sick people for selfish reasons.

tropes.name: Won't Do Your Dirty Work
tropes.def: The hero/villain is told to solve his own problems.

tropes.name: Working the Same Case
tropes.def: Two teams who are investigating the same case.

tropes.name: Workplace Horror
tropes.def: A setting where unexpected horrors appear while trying do to a mundane job.

tropes.name: World-Healing Wave
tropes.def: A wave envelopes the world to heal it from all the damage and corruption.

tropes.name: World Tour
tropes.def: The characters travel to well-known places around the world.

tropes.name: Worst Wedding Ever
tropes.def: Someone's wedding turns disastrous.

tropes.name: Wounded Gazelle Gambit
tropes.def: Manipulating people by pretending to be injured.

tropes.name: Wounded Gazelle Warcry
tropes.def: The weakest combatant rushes in harm's way to motivate the others into action.

tropes.name: Wrong Time-Travel Savvy
tropes.def: Someone mistakenly thinks they know how time travel works.

tropes.name: Wrong Turn at Albuquerque
tropes.def: A single wrong turn lands the traveler in a place far from their original goal.

tropes.name: Wunza Plot
tropes.def: A plot with two characters who are very different and team up to accomplish a goal.

tropes.name: X Must Not Win
tropes.def: Wanting to avoid letting a particular character be victorious provides fuel for the other character's persistence in fighting against them.

tropes.name: Xanatos Gambit
tropes.def: A plan for which all foreseeable outcomes benefit the creator — including ones that superficially appear to be failure.

tropes.name: Xanatos Speed Chess
tropes.def: Quickly altering plans as needed.

tropes.name: Yank the Dog's Chain
tropes.def: Right when it looks like this unfortunate person will finally have better luck, their chances at happiness are ruined at the last minute.

tropes.name: Yearning for a Nemesis
tropes.def: A character desires to find a nemesis.

tropes.name: Yellow Brick Road
tropes.def: The pathway a character has to travel along to get to their ultimate goal.

tropes.name: You All Meet in a Cell
tropes.def: Characters meet while they're all captive, and learn why they were taken captive in the first place while they escape.

tropes.name: You All Meet in an Inn
tropes.def: Everyone meets when they're at the same inn.

tropes.name: You Already Changed the Past
tropes.def: Someone attempts to prevent an atrocity from happening in the past, only to find in the end that the atrocity wouldn't have happened in the first place if they didn't go back in time to try and prevent it.

tropes.name: You Are the New Trend
tropes.def: A character's distinctive look or mannerisms becomes the model for the latest hot trend.

tropes.name: You Can Keep Her!
tropes.def: A character is contacted by some kidnappers who are holding someone they should care about for ransom, but the character doesn't care.

tropes.name: You Go, Girl!
tropes.def: A girl proves that she's as good as the boys in athletics.

tropes.name: You Have Waited Long Enough
tropes.def: A character is forced to marry someone else when the one they love doesn't come right back to them.

tropes.name: You Know What You Did
tropes.def: A character assumes the worst about someone without bothering to confirm it.

tropes.name: You Wake Up in a Room
tropes.def: A character wakes up in an unfamiliar place at the beginning of the story.

tropes.name: You Wake Up on a Beach
tropes.def: Someone wakes up on the beach with no recollection of how they got there.

tropes.name: Youngest Child Wins
tropes.def: The youngest sibling has the best luck in life.

tropes.name: Yo-Yo Plot Point
tropes.def: A premise-changing plot point is resolved and unresolved several times over the course of the work.

tropes.name: Zany Scheme
tropes.def: One or more characters tries to achieve some end — usually extricating themselves from trouble — by some kind of elaborate, unlikely plan.

tropes.name: Zany Scheme Chicken
tropes.def: An escalating war of zany schemes, which grow progressively more absurd.

tropes.name: Zombie Apocalypse
tropes.def: The world ends via being overrun by the undead.
